name: 74LS390 Dual 4-bit Decade Counter IC DIP-16
desc: The 74LS390 is a dual decade counter IC containing two independent divide-by-2 and divide-by-5 counters, used for frequency division.

blocks.text: The 74LS390 is a monolithic integrated circuit from the Texas Instruments LS (Low-Power Schottky) family, designed as a dual, independent 4-bit decade counter. This single package effectively contains two separate counter units, each built with internal master-slave flip-flops and additional gating logic. Its primary function is to count electronic pulses, and it is specifically configured to count in decades, meaning each counter cycles through ten distinct states (0-9) before resetting. This dual configuration is a key design aspect, aimed at significantly increasing system density by reducing the number of individual IC packages required for counting tasks.

Each of the two internal counters within the 74LS390 is not a single 4-bit counter but is itself composed of two smaller counters: a divide-by-2 section and a divide-by-5 section. These sub-counters have individual clock inputs (1CKA and 1CKB for the first counter, for example), providing flexibility in how the counting sequence is configured. The outputs of these sections can be interconnected in various ways, allowing each counter to implement different division ratios, including a full divide-by-10 sequence or a bi-quinary count (2 and 5) to produce a symmetrical square wave at the final output.

The device includes a direct clear (reset) input for each 4-bit counter, allowing for the immediate and asynchronous reset of the count to zero, independent of the clock signal. All outputs are buffered, which enhances output drive capability and reduces the possibility of noise issues during signal transitions. Characterized for operation from 0°C to 70°C, it is intended for use in commercial and industrial electronic systems where reliable, medium-speed counting and frequency division are required.

blocks.text: 74LS221 IC-Dual Non-Retrigger able-Monostable Multivibrator With Reset

The 74LS221 (74221) is a dual non-retrigger able monostable multivibrator that provides two independent one-shot circuits in a single 16-pin package. Each channel accepts both negative-transition and positive-transition trigger inputs, enabling flexible triggering schemes for diverse digital designs. Schmitt-triggered B inputs and internal latching give the device excellent noise immunity and predictable triggering behaviour.

Pulse width is set by external timing components (Rext and Cext) and follows the approximate relationship tw ≈ 0.7·Rext·Cext, allowing pulse durations from tens of nanoseconds up to milliseconds depending on component values. Once a pulse is initiated the output remains independent of further A/B input transitions (non-retriggerable), while an overriding clear input (CLR) can terminate the pulse early when required. Timing stability is ensured across supply and temperature ranges by internal compensation.

The device offers TTL-compatible rise/fall times and totem-pole outputs, and is available in multiple packages (PDIP, SOIC, SSOP, CDIP, etc.), making it straightforward to integrate in through-hole and surface-mount assemblies. Common uses include reset generation, pulse stretching, debouncing, and timing control where a compact, reliable single-shot solution is needed.

desc: Low-power CMOS ICM7555 timer (DIP-8) 4.5–15V operation, ~80µA standby, 500kHz max, TTL/CMOS compatible outputs for astable/monostable timing.

blocks.text: ICM7555 General Purpose CMOS Timer DIP

The ICM7555 is a low-power CMOS implementation of the industry-standard 555 timer in a compact DIP-8 package. It is designed to produce accurate time delays and stable oscillations using only a few external components. Compared with bipolar 555 devices, the ICM7555 significantly reduces quiescent current and power-spike behavior during output transitions, making it a better fit for battery-powered and low-power instrumentation.

In operation the chip can be configured as either a monostable (one-shot) or astable (oscillator) timer; a single resistor–capacitor pair controls timing in monostable mode, while two resistors plus a capacitor set frequency and duty cycle in astable mode. The device provides TTL/CMOS-compatible output levels at 5 V and maintains stable timing characteristics across its recommended supply range, simplifying integration into mixed-logic systems.

Mechanically offered in DIP-8, SOP-8, MSOP-8 and DFN-8 packages, the ICM7555 balances compact footprint with straightforward through-hole or surface-mount assembly. Its low leakage on trigger/threshold/reset pins, modest thermal ratings and predictable switching times make it useful for a wide range of control and timing tasks where low standby current and stable timing are important.

name: MT8870DS DTMF Receiver SMD IC
desc: Manufacturer MICROCHIP Mfr. Part # MT8870DS Package SOIC-18-300mil Datasheet MT8870DS Description 15mW SOIC-18-300mil Telecom RoHS

blocks.text: The MT8870DS is a complete, monolithic Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF) receiver integrated circuit. Its primary role is to accurately detect and decode the standard 16 DTMF tone pairs, which are the combinations of high and low-frequency tones used in telephone signaling, into a corresponding 4-bit binary code. This IC elegantly integrates both the essential bandsplit filter and the digital decoder functions onto a single chip, providing a highly compact solution for telephony and control systems.

The device employs a sophisticated architecture for reliable signal interpretation. The incoming DTMF signal is first processed by a filter section that uses switched capacitor techniques to cleanly separate the low and high-group tones. This section also incorporates notches to reject common dial tones, preventing false triggering. The separated tones are then passed to a digital decoder that uses a complex averaging algorithm to verify the frequencies and their duration, ensuring immunity to voice simulation and noise.

Designed for easy integration into larger systems, the MT8870DS minimizes external component requirements by including an on-chip differential input amplifier, clock oscillator, and a latched three-state bus interface. It offers designer flexibility through features like an adjustable guard time for validating signal duration, a power-down mode for energy savings, and an inhibit mode to ignore specific tone codes. The three-state outputs allow for direct connection to a microprocessor data bus.

A key characteristic of the HM-10 is its ability to operate in both master and slave roles, enabling it to initiate connections to other devices or accept incoming connections. The module supports three distinct work modes: a transparent transmission mode for bidirectional data exchange, a remote control mode for managing the output states of its I/O pins, and a PIO acquisition mode for monitoring sensor or switch inputs. It also features intelligent power management, including a sleep mode that can be woken via a specific data string or a system key, ensuring efficient operation in battery-powered applications.

desc: The GS8334 is a quad, zero-drift CMOS op-amp with rail-to-rail I/O, 350kHz bandwidth, and ultra-low 10µV offset.

blocks.text: The GS8334 is a quad, micro-power, zero-drift CMOS operational amplifier that utilizes a chopper-stabilized technique. This advanced design methodology is fundamental to its performance, actively correcting the input offset voltage to achieve an exceptionally low and stable error over time and temperature.

The General Instrument 27C128 is a CMOS-based ultraviolet light erasable programmable read-only memory. With a total capacity of 128K bits, it is organized as 16,384 words by 8 bits, effectively functioning as a 16-kilobyte non-volatile storage device. This architecture allows it to store firmware or permanent data for a microprocessor-based system, holding its content without power.

The device is designed for fully static operation, requiring no clocks or refresh cycles, which simplifies its integration into a system. Accessing a byte of data, whether from a change in address or when the chip is enabled, is accomplished with high speed. The CMOS design is a key characteristic, enabling the chip to consume very little power, especially in standby mode where the current drops dramatically.

Data is written to the memory through an electrical programming process that requires a higher programming voltage on the Vpp pin. The stored data can be erased entirely by exposing the quartz window on the chip package to ultraviolet light, which resets all bits to a logical ‘1’ state. The chip includes control inputs for Chip Enable and Output Enable, allowing for easy connection to a system bus and preventing bus contention.

This microcontroller serves as a powerful, monolithic chip that integrates a versatile 8-bit Central Processing Unit (CPU) with Flash memory, forming a complete embedded system on a single piece of silicon.

name: TL16C750FN – 3.3V/5V Single UART with 64-Byte FIFOs and Auto-Flow Control SMD IC
desc: Manufacturer Texas Instruments Mfr. Part # TL16C750FN Package FN – 44-pin PLCC Datasheet TL16C750FN Description The TL16C750FN is a 3.3V/5V UART with 64-byte FIFOs

blocks.text: TL16C750FN – 3.3V/5V Single UART with 64-Byte FIFOs and Auto-Flow Control SMD IC

The TL16C750FN is an Asynchronous Communications Element (ACE), commonly known as a UART, which serves as a crucial interface between a parallel data bus and a serial communication channel. It performs serial-to-parallel conversion on data received from peripheral devices and parallel-to-serial conversion on data transmitted from its central processing unit (CPU). This device is a functional upgrade of earlier models, maintaining full software compatibility while introducing advanced features to reduce CPU overhead and enhance data integrity in serial communication systems.

A key advancement of the TL16C750FN is its integrated buffering system. It incorporates 64-byte FIFOs (First-In, First-Out) for both the receiver and transmitter sections. These FIFOs temporarily store data, allowing the CPU to handle data in blocks rather than on a character-by-character basis. This buffering significantly reduces the number of interrupts the CPU must service, thereby lowering software overhead and increasing overall system efficiency and performance in data-intensive applications.

To further optimize data flow and prevent data loss, the TL16C750FN features a programmable auto-flow control mechanism. This system is composed of auto-RTS (Request To Send) and auto-CTS (Clear To Send). Auto-RTS automatically desserts the RTS signal when the receiver FIFO is nearing capacity, signaling the transmitting device to pause. Conversely, auto-CTS halts the transmitter if the CTS signal is inactive, indicating the receiving device is not ready. This hardware-managed handshake eliminates overrun errors without CPU intervention.

name: P6KE440 600W 440V UNIDIRECTIONAL TVS Diode
desc: The P6KE440 is a 600W unidirectional TVS diode designed to protect circuits by clamping 440V voltage transients to a safe level with a fast response time.

blocks.text: The P6KE440 is a Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diode engineered to protect sensitive electronic components from damaging voltage transients. As a unidirectional device, it is designed to clamp voltage spikes in one polarity, specifically when a positive voltage surge exceeds the circuit’s normal operating range. Its primary role is to act as a robust electronic shield, diverting excessive transient current away from vulnerable circuits.

When a sudden over-voltage event, such as an electrostatic discharge (ESD) or inductive load switching spike, occurs, the P6KE440 reacts almost instantaneously. It shifts from a high-impedance state to a low-impedance state, effectively clamping the voltage to a safe, predetermined level. This action safely dissipates the high peak pulse energy, rated at 600 watts, through the diode, thereby maintaining the voltage across the protected circuit within its safe operating limits.

Housed in a DO-15 (also known as DO-204AC) package, this diode is physically robust and designed for straightforward PCB mounting. The component is marked for polarity identification, which is crucial for the correct installation of the unidirectional type. It is constructed from materials with a UL 94V-0 flammability rating and is compliant with major industry regulations concerning hazardous substances and supply chain ethics.

desc: A 24.000MHz fundamental frequency quartz crystal in a standard HC-49/U through-hole package, providing a precise and stable clock signal for digital circuits.

blocks.text: The HC49/U is a through-hole quartz crystal resonator housed in a standard HC-49/U package. This package is a classic, leaded metal casing that provides robustness and stability for the enclosed quartz crystal blank. The component is designed for wave soldering onto printed circuit boards and is not moisture sensitive, which simplifies storage and handling processes. Its construction involves resistance welding, ensuring a reliable and hermetic seal to protect the sensitive internal element from environmental factors.

This specific component is calibrated to a fundamental frequency of 24.000 MHz. Operating at its fundamental frequency means that the crystal’s oscillation is based on its primary, natural mechanical resonance. This is in contrast to overtone modes, which are higher harmonics of the fundamental frequency. The fundamental mode operation is typically chosen for frequencies up to approximately 24 MHz, making this crystal a standard choice for clock generation in many digital circuits within this frequency range.

The crystal’s primary function is to generate a highly precise and stable clock signal. Its performance is characterized by key parameters such as frequency tolerance and stability over a specified temperature range. For a 24.000 MHz crystal, it requires an external load capacitance to operate at its specified frequency, with a standard value of 18 pF. The crystal is designed to maintain its oscillation integrity within defined limits of drive level and equivalent series resistance, ensuring consistent performance in the target application.

desc: The 74HC251 is a high-speed CMOS 8-input digital multiplexer with 3-state outputs. It selects one of eight data lines using a 3-bit address.

blocks.text: 74HC251 74251 Signal Switches, Multiplexers, Decoder IC PDIP-16

The 74HC251 is a high-speed CMOS integrated circuit that functions as an 8-input digital multiplexer. Its primary role is to select one of eight binary data inputs and route it to a single output channel. This data selection is controlled by a 3-bit binary address, making it a fundamental building block for managing multiple data streams in digital systems, effectively acting as a digitally-controlled signal switch.

A key feature of this IC is its provision of both true (Y) and complemented (W) data outputs, offering immediate logic-level flexibility for the selected signal. Furthermore, the outputs are three-state, meaning they can be put into a high-impedance (high-Z) mode. This is controlled by a dedicated Output Enable pin; when this pin is inactive, both outputs disconnect from the internal circuit, allowing multiple devices to be connected to a shared bus without interference.

Fabricated with advanced silicon-gate CMOS technology, the 74HC251 offers the high noise immunity and low power consumption typical of CMOS devices, while achieving speeds comparable to LSTTL logic. It operates over a wide supply voltage range and is designed to interface directly with other CMOS series, as well as NMOS and TTL components, providing versatility in mixed-logic system design.

desc: The TP80C31BH is a low-power CHMOS 8-bit microcontroller from the MCS-51 family in a 40-pin DIP package.

blocks.text: The TP80C31BH is a single-chip, control-oriented 8-bit microcontroller fabricated using Intel’s reliable CHMOS III-E technology. As a member of the MCS®-51 family, it maintains full architectural and instruction set compatibility with this established lineage. This device is designed as a general-purpose embedded control unit, integrating the core CPU, timing logic, and interrupt control on a single piece of silicon to form a complete microcomputer system.

This microcontroller is characterized by its lack of on-chip program memory, requiring all program code to be stored externally. It features 128 bytes of on-chip data RAM for efficient variable handling and stack operations. The device can address up to 64K bytes of both external program and external data memory, facilitated by its multiplexed address and data bus on Port 0 and the high-order address bus on Port 2, providing significant flexibility for system expansion.

A key characteristic of the TP80C31BH is its low power consumption, enhanced by two software-selectable power-saving modes. Idle mode halts the CPU while allowing the RAM, timers, serial port, and interrupt system to remain active. Power Down mode preserves RAM contents but stops the oscillator, reducing power to a minimal level. These features make it particularly suitable for battery-powered or energy-sensitive applications where power efficiency is critical.

blocks.text: The MAX192BCPP is a fully integrated, low-cost data-acquisition system. desc: The IRFP9240 is a -200V P-Channel MOSFET in a TO-247 package with a low 0.34Ω on-resistance. It’s designed for fast switching, is avalanche-rated.

blocks.text: The IRFP9240 is a silicon P-channel enhanced mode power MOSFET, manufactured using advanced MOSFET technology. This technology is focused on optimizing key performance parameters, specifically engineered to significantly reduce conduction losses during operation. The fundamental structure is a vertical DMOS design, which allows it to handle high voltage and current efficiently. As a P-channel device, its voltage polarities and current flow are the inverse of the more common N-channel MOSFETs, making it suitable for specific circuit configurations like high-side switching.

A primary benefit of this transistor’s advanced design is its improved switching performance, making it effective in high-frequency applications. The device is characterized by a low on-resistance, which directly contributes to higher efficiency by minimizing power loss when the transistor is in its fully on state. Furthermore, it has been ruggedized, featuring an enhanced dv/dt capability and being 100% tested for avalanche energy, meaning it can withstand stressful transient voltage spikes without failing, thus improving system reliability.

Housed in the robust TO-247 package, the IRFP9240 is built for high power dissipation. This package facilitates easy and secure mounting to an external heat sink, which is crucial for managing the thermal load generated during operation in power-intensive applications. The combination of its electrical characteristics and physical packaging makes it a component designed for durability and performance in demanding environments like switch-mode power supplies.

name: P8049AH Microcontroller IC DIP-40
desc: The Intel P8049AH is an HMOS single-chip 8-bit microcontroller with 2KB ROM, 128B RAM, 27 I/O lines, & a timer counter, designed for efficient embedded control

blocks.text: The Intel P8049AH is a high-performance, single-component 8-bit microcontroller fabricated with HMOS II technology. It is a fully self-sufficient parallel computer integrated onto a single silicon chip, designed to serve as an efficient controller and arithmetic processor. Its core includes an 8-bit CPU, an on-board oscillator, and clock circuits, allowing it to form the heart of a compact control system with minimal external components. The architecture is optimized for control tasks with extensive bit-handling capabilities and support for both binary and BCD arithmetic.

This microcontroller contains its own program and data memory on-chip, featuring 2K x 8 bits of Mask ROM and 128 x 8 bits of RAM. This integrated memory allows the processor to execute its instruction set—which consists mostly of single-byte instructions for efficient memory use—directly from internal storage. The design includes an 8-bit timer/counter that can function as an interval timer or an event counter, adding to its capability for creating precise timing delays or counting external pulses without external hardware.

For systems requiring extra capability, the P8049AH is designed for easy expansion. It provides 27 I/O lines, organized into ports and a bidirectional bus, which can be used to interface with a wide range of peripherals. The memory and I/O can be expanded using standard MCS-80/MCS-85 peripherals. Control signals like ALE, PSEN, RD, and WR facilitate this expansion, allowing the microcontroller to manage external program memory, data memory, and additional I/O ports seamlessly.

blocks.text: The D80C49C is a high-speed, single-chip CMOS microcomputer that integrates a complete 8-bit computing system onto one piece of silicon. Its core comprises an 8-bit CPU, which efficiently executes a set of 98 instructions. The architecture includes an Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) capable of arithmetic, logic, and decimal adjust functions, an accumulator for data manipulation, and two sets of working registers for efficient context switching. This integrated design provides a self-contained processing unit for embedded control tasks.

This microcontroller features 2K bytes of on-chip mask-programmable ROM for program storage and 256 bytes of RAM for data handling. It includes sophisticated control circuitry for managing operations, including an internal timer/event counter for generating precise delays or counting external pulses. The system supports an 8-level stack for subroutine handling and features interrupt capability for responsive event-driven programming. It can also single-step through instructions, which is a valuable feature for system debugging and development.

Fabricated using CMOS technology, the D80C49C is designed for low power consumption. It employs advanced standby functions, including HALT and STOP modes, to minimize power drain significantly during inactive periods. The device operates from a single power supply ranging from +2.5V to +6.0V. For system expansion, it offers expandable memory and I/O ports, utilizing a bidirectional data bus and dedicated control signals like ALE, RD, and WR to interface with external components.

name: LM301AN Operational Amplifier DIP-8
desc: LM301AN single, general-purpose DIP-8 operational amplifier with external compensation, wide ±5V–±22V supply range, low drift and flexible bandwidth.

blocks.text: The LM301AN is a classic, single-package operational amplifier offered in an 8-pin DIP (DIP-8) that serves as a flexible building block for analogue designs. It’s built for general-purpose amplification across a wide supply range (±5 V to ±22 V), and was designed so the external compensation capacitor can be tailored to the application. This means designers can optimize stability, bandwidth and slew response for a given circuit instead of relying on fixed internal compensation.

In normal operation the LM301AN performs as a low-drift, low-noise amplifier with modest input currents and millivolt-level offset. It provides useful open-loop gain, predictable common-mode behavior and protection against overloads on the input and output so that it remains robust in many bench and field circuits. The device can be used as a voltage follower, small-signal amplifier, or as the active element in filters and integrators.

Mechanically the LM301AN is supplied in a standard plastic DIP-8 footprint with the pinout and package dimensions suitable for through-hole prototyping and legacy PCBs. Its external compensation (single 30 pF shown in datasheet examples) and tolerant input range let engineers trade off slew rate, bandwidth and stability to meet application needs. The LM301AN remains a simple, adaptable op-amp for educational, hobbyist and many industrial uses.

blocks.text: The D8741AD is a programmable peripheral interface controller, designed as a complete, self-sufficient 8-bit single-chip microcomputer. It features its own CPU, UV-EPROM program memory, and RAM, allowing it to operate as an intelligent slave device. Its primary role is to offload input/output (I/O) handling and peripheral control tasks from a master CPU, thereby increasing the overall efficiency of a microprocessor-based system.

This IC is engineered for seamless integration into master/slave configurations with various 8-bit and 16-bit microprocessors like the 8048, 8085A, and 8086. It communicates with the host processor through an asynchronous interface that includes a bidirectional data bus, status registers, and control lines (RD, WR). This structure allows for flexible data exchange via interrupt, DMA, or polled operation methods.

At its core, the D8741AD contains 1K bytes of user-programmable UV-EPROM and 64 bytes of RAM. It is equipped with 18 I/O lines organized into two ports, an 8-bit timer/counter, and a clock circuit. name: BDW94C PNP Darlington Transistor 12A 100V TO-220
desc: The BDW94C is a -12A, -100V PNP Darlington power transistor in a TO-220 package. It is the complementary pair to the BDW93C.

blocks.text: The BDW94C is a robust silicon power transistor engineered using an Epitaxial-Base PNP process and configured in a monolithic Darlington arrangement. This design integrates two transistors into a single device, resulting in a component capable of delivering very high current gain. It is specifically intended for demanding roles in both power linear amplification and high-speed switching circuits, making it a versatile solution for controlling significant power levels in industrial environments.

The transistor is constructed in a monolithic Darlington configuration, which internally pairs two bipolar transistors to multiply the current gain, allowing a small base current to control a much larger collector current. This entire assembly is securely housed in a industry-standard Jedec TO-220 plastic package. This package is renowned for its mechanical durability and excellent thermal performance, facilitating easy mounting to a heat sink to manage the substantial power dissipation during operation.

A key feature of its design is the integration of an antiparallel collector-emitter diode within the same monolithic structure. This internal diode provides inherent protection against voltage spikes in inductive load applications. Furthermore, the BDW94C is offered as the direct PNP complement to the BDW93C NPN transistor, which simplifies the design of push-pull output stages and other symmetrical circuits.

name: Network Resistor 330 ohm 9 pin
desc: A 330 ohm, 9-pin single common resistor network in a compact SIP. Features a 2% tolerance and 0.125W rating for space-efficient circuit design.

blocks.text: The 330 ohm 9-pin resistor network is a highly integrated component that consolidates multiple resistors into a single, compact Single-In-Line Package (SIP). This design is fundamental for achieving miniaturization and high component density on modern printed circuit boards. By replacing several discrete resistors with one unified part, it streamlines the assembly process, reduces the bill of materials, and enhances overall circuit reliability by minimizing the number of solder joints, which are potential points of failure.

This 9-pin component is configured with a “Single Common” circuit type, identified by the letter ‘A’. In this arrangement, one of the nine pins serves as a common bus or shared connection point. The remaining eight pins are each connected to their own individual resistor, all of which are linked to this common bus. This architecture is exceptionally efficient for applications where multiple circuit lines require a common reference point, such as a set of pull-up or pull-down resistors.

Constructed with high-reliability materials including RU02 paste, this network ensures stable and consistent electrical performance. The device is clearly marked with a code like “A331G” on its body. This marking provides immediate identification of its single-common circuit architecture, confirms the 330-ohm resistance value for each of the eight resistors, and specifies a precise manufacturing tolerance of ±2%, ensuring accuracy in the end application.

This design is pivotal for modern electronics, where board real estate is at a premium. By combining eight discrete components into one, it significantly reduces the part count on a PCB, which not only saves space but also enhances manufacturing efficiency and improves overall circuit reliability by minimizing potential failure points associated with numerous individual soldering joints.

This 8-pin network is designed with an “Isolated” circuit architecture, denoted by the letter ‘B’. In this configuration, each of the resistors is entirely independent of the others, with no internal common connection. This provides a circuit designer with maximum flexibility, allowing each 100K ohm resistor to be deployed in separate and unrelated parts of a circuit simultaneously, just as if eight separate through-hole resistors were being used, but with the significant benefits of integrated packaging.

Manufactured with a focus on durability and consistent performance, this network utilizes high-reliability materials like RU02 paste. The component is clearly identified by a marking such as “B104G” on its body. desc: 256K-bit (32K×8) CMOS EPROM (27C256) fast reads (90 ns option), low power, express programming, multiple packages (DIP/PLCC/SOIC), wide temp ranges.

blocks.text: The 27C256 is a 256-Kbit (32K × 8) CMOS EPROM (one-time programmable) designed for high-speed, low-power read operations. It provides fast, byte-wide access (access times down to 90 ns) so microprocessors can fetch code or data without added wait states. The device is offered in multiple package styles (DIP, PLCC, SOIC) and supports standard JEDEC pinouts for easy board integration.

Built using CMOS technology, the 27C256 minimizes active and standby current draw (typical active ≈20 mA; standby ≈100 µA) while maintaining stable output drive and low leakage. Programming is performed using a VPP programming voltage and an express programming algorithm that applies short program pulses and verifies bytes automatically, improving production throughput. The device also includes separate CE and OE controls to simplify bus sharing and system designs.

The part is robust for long-term storage (data retention >200 years specified) and is available across commercial, industrial and automotive temperature ranges, making it suitable for legacy systems, firmware storage, and environments that require extended temperature operation. Identity mode and programming inhibit features ease manufacturing and parallel programming setups.

blocks.text: The M27C512 is a 512 Kbit Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory (EPROM) integrated circuit, organized in a 65,536 x 8-bit structure. It is offered in two primary variants: an ultraviolet (UV) erasable version, which allows for multiple reprogramming cycles, and a One Time Programmable (OTP) version for permanent code storage. The device is designed to provide a reliable and flexible non-volatile memory solution for systems where fast development and code experimentation are critical.

The chip’s operation is managed through a two-line control system consisting of Chip Enable (E) and Output Enable (G). This architecture is ideal for use in larger memory arrays, as it minimizes power dissipation and prevents output bus contention. The M27C512 features a low-power CMOS standby mode, significantly reducing current consumption when the device is not selected. For programming, it utilizes a specialized algorithm and requires a specific programming voltage to write data into the memory cells.

The device is available in several packages, including the PDIP28 (Plastic Dual In-line Package) which is a through-hole design. The UV-erasable version comes in a ceramic package (FDIP28W) with a transparent window. Exposing this window to short-wave ultraviolet light erases the entire memory content, resetting all bits to a logical ‘1’ state and preparing the device for a new program cycle, a key feature for development and debugging.

name: Metal Oxide Varistor 14D221K MOV
desc: The 14D221K is a 220V metal oxide varistor that provides robust overvoltage protection by clamping transient surges and absorbing high energy pulses up to 4500A

blocks.text: The 14D221K is a protective electronic component designed to safeguard circuits from voltage transients. Its operation is defined by its highly non-linear electrical characteristic. Under normal operating conditions, where the voltage remains below its threshold, it exhibits a very high electrical resistance, making it virtually invisible to the circuit. However, when a sudden voltage spike occurs, its resistance drops dramatically within nanoseconds.

This device is constructed from a ceramic mass of zinc oxide (ZnO) grains mixed with other metal oxides, forming the core varistor element. The boundaries between these zinc oxide grains are responsible for the component’s ability to clamp over-voltages. This sintered ceramic disk is then packaged within a flame-retardant epoxy resin coating, which provides both mechanical robustness and electrical insulation, making it suitable for demanding environments.

The primary purpose of the 14D221K is to divert the dangerous surge current away from sensitive components, thereby limiting the voltage across the circuit to a safe, predetermined level known as the clamping voltage. By providing a low-impedance path to ground during an over-voltage event, it absorbs the transient energy and dissipates it as heat, effectively sacrificing itself to protect the rest of the system.

However, when a transient over-voltage event occurs and exceeds its specific threshold, the varistor instantly switches to a state of very low impedance.

This device is a multilayer structure composed primarily of zinc oxide (ZnO) grains mixed with other metal oxides, forming the bulk of the ceramic element. These grains create a network of semiconductor junctions, which are responsible for the component’s unique current-voltage characteristics. The entire element is encased in a robust, flame-retardant epoxy resin coating, ensuring mechanical integrity and electrical isolation.

The critical action of the 07D391K is to clamp transient voltages to a safe, predetermined level, thereby diverting the potentially damaging surge current away from vulnerable components. By absorbing and dissipating the energy from voltage spikes as heat, it effectively limits the voltage across its terminals to a maximum clamping value, ensuring the downstream circuitry remains within its safe operating voltage range.

The KA3842 is a high-performance current-mode PWM controller IC designed for off-line and DC-DC converter applications that require high efficiency, precision control, and fast response. It operates as a fixed-frequency controller and provides all the essential functions needed for implementing reliable and cost-effective switch-mode power supplies (SMPS). With a wide operating voltage range of 7.6 V to 30 V and a precision 5.0 V reference, the KA3842 delivers stable operation across a variety of input conditions.

Featuring a high-speed totem-pole output, the KA3842 can directly drive power MOSFETs or BJTs with peak currents up to 1 A, ensuring efficient switching and reduced power losses. Its current-mode control architecture provides superior line and load regulation, automatic pulse-by-pulse current limiting, and inherent cycle-by-cycle overcurrent protection.

The KA3842 includes undervoltage lockout (UVLO) with typical start and stop thresholds of 16 V and 10 V, making it particularly well suited for off-line (AC-to-DC) power supplies and continuous conduction mode designs. Housed in a compact DIP-8 package, it offers a cost-effective solution for applications such as industrial power supplies, motor drivers, and battery chargers that demand robust, efficient PWM control.
Wide Operating Voltage Range: 7.6 V to 30 V.
Precision 5.0 V Reference: ±2% tolerance for accurate regulation.
Fixed-Frequency Operation: Up to 500 kHz (set by external RT/CT).
Current-Mode Control: Provides superior line and load regulation with cycle-by-cycle current limiting.
High-Speed Totem-Pole Output: ±1 A peak drive capability for direct MOSFET or transistor control.
Low Start-Up Current: Less than 0.5 mA for high-efficiency standby operation.
Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO): Start-up at 16 V, turn-off at 10 V for off-line power applications.
Built-In Soft-Start and Leading-Edge Blanking: Enhances system stability and noise immunity.
Thermal Stability: Ensures consistent performance over temperature range.
Standard 8-Pin DIP/SOP Package: Simplifies design integration and PCB layout.

blocks.text: 4505 64-BIT, 1-BIT PER WORD RANDOM ACCESS MEMORY (RAM) DIP-14

The HEF4505B is a fully decoded, static 64-bit random access memory implemented as 1-bit per word cells in a 14-lead DIP package. Designed in Philips’ LOCMOS process, it provides simple, low-power storage for small memories where density is low but access control and robustness matter. The device exposes six address lines to select one of 64 locations, a single data input, and a single data output, plus dedicated control pins for strobe and chip enables.

Reads and writes occur only when the strobe (ST) and chip-enable inputs (CE1 and CE2) are asserted appropriately, allowing precise timing control and easy expansion by tying outputs together. The output goes to a defined low state before data becomes valid and can be placed in a high-impedance OFF state for bus sharing. Very low leakage and standby dissipation make the HEF4505B attractive for battery-sustained or trickle-charged backup arrangements.

Because the memory is static and fully decoded, no external refresh is required and system wiring is straightforward. Typical use emphasizes small lookup tables, register storage, and low-power nonvolatile-style retention (with a small battery) rather than high-density storage. The DIP-14 form factor and standard pinout simplify prototyping and replacements in legacy boards.

blocks.text: MAX712CPE+ Multi-Chemical 1~16 P DIP-16 Battery Management IC

The MAX712CPE+ is a specialized integrated circuit designed to manage the fast charging of Nickel-Metal Hydride (NiMH) and Nickel-Cadmium (NiCd) battery packs. It operates as a sophisticated controller that regulates the charging process from a DC power source, ensuring batteries are charged efficiently and safely. The chip is capable of handling battery configurations ranging from 1 to 16 cells connected in series, making it highly versatile for various battery-powered devices.

The primary role of the MAX712 is to conduct a constant-current fast-charge cycle, which can occur at rates as high as 4C. Its intelligent charging algorithm determines when the battery is fully charged by monitoring multiple parameters. Unlike the MAX713 which detects a negative voltage slope, the MAX712 is designed to terminate the fast charge upon detecting a zero voltage slope (∆V/∆t=0). It also incorporates temperature window comparators and a programmable timer as backup termination methods to prevent overcharging.

Housed in a standard 16-pin PDIP package, the device is powered through an on-board 5V shunt regulator from the DC input. It features a low-side current-sense resistor, allowing it to regulate the charge current even while simultaneously powering the system’s load from the same source. When not actively charging, the IC draws a minimal current of only 5µA from the battery, preserving its charge. It can be configured for either linear or more efficient switch-mode power control.

name: 74123 Dual Retriggerable Monostable Multivibrator With Clear DIP-16 IC
desc: 74123 A dual, retrigger able one-shot multivibrator IC in a 16-pin DIP. Generates precise output pulses with a width set by external RC components.

blocks.text: 74123 Dual Retrigger able Monostable Multivibrator With Clear DIP-16 IC

The 74123 is a monolithic integrated circuit that contains two independent retrigger able monostable multivibrators in a single DIP-16 package. A monostable multivibrator, also known as a “one-shot,” is a circuit that produces a single output pulse of a predetermined duration each time it is triggered by an external signal. This chip is designed to generate precise, timed intervals from transient input signals.

The device offers significant flexibility in how it is triggered and controlled. Each multivibrator features both active-low (A) and active-high (B) trigger inputs, allowing it to be initiated by either a rising or falling edge from gated logic signals. A key characteristic is its retrigger able capability, which allows the output pulse to be extended by applying a new trigger before the initial timing period expires. Furthermore, an overriding Clear input provides immediate termination of the output pulse.

The duration of the output pulse is not fixed internally but is programmed by connecting external timing components a resistor (R_T) and a capacitor (C_ext). This allows the pulse width to be tailored from nanoseconds to seconds, making the chip highly versatile. The output is provided in both true (Q) and complementary (Q̅) forms, offering additional logic flexibility for system design.
Contains Two Independent Retrigger able Monostables.
DC Triggering from Active-High or Active-Low Inputs.
Output Pulse Duration Controlled by External RC Network.

blocks.text: Carbon Monoxide (CO) Gas Sensor RS-COWS-N01-2-2000P-5 RS485

The RS-COWS-N01-2-2000P-5 (RS485) is a smart CO gas transmitter combining gas, temperature and humidity sensing in one unit. Its compact and modular design enables installation on walls or panels in industrial or building control contexts, with the ability to network multiple units via the RS-485 bus.

When powered (10–30 V DC), the unit initializes and stabilizes, then begins measuring ambient CO concentration, ambient temperature, and humidity at periodic intervals (every 2 seconds). This digital communication mitigates the signal degradation and noise susceptibility that often affects analogue transmissions over distance.

In a networked monitoring system, multiple units can share a common RS-485 line, each with a unique address. The central controller (PLC, SCADA, BMS) polls each sensor for its current readings and can trigger actions (ventilation, alarms) based on threshold crossings. The integrated multi-parameter sensing in one package simplifies deployment and wiring, making it suitable for continuous environmental safety monitoring in parking garages, mechanical rooms, laboratories, or HVAC zones.

name: Soldering Wire 0.6mm|100Gm (Alloy:63/37) Made in China
desc: 63/37 rosin-core solder wire, 0.6 mm diameter, 100 g spool melts at 183 °C, reliable for electronics, good flow and wetting in compact joints.

blocks.text: This soldering wire is a thin, flexible metallic filament, carefully wound into a spool weighing 100 g. With a diameter of 0.6 mm, it offers a precise and controlled feed when soldering delicate electronics or circuit boards. The alloy is composed of 63 % tin and 37 % lead, a classic eutectic mixture known for its sharp melting point and reliable solder flow behavior.

Embedded within the metal is a rosin flux core, which activates when heated and helps clean oxide layers on component leads and copper pads. As the wire melts, the flux promotes wetting and adhesion of the solder to both surfaces, reducing the need for external flux in many cases. The wire’s surface is smooth and uniform, ensuring consistent melting and deposition of solder without abrupt spurts or gaps.

In practice, a technician unwinds a small length of this wire to feed into the joint being soldered. The soldering iron tip touches the joint and the wire simultaneously: the heat melts the wire and lets it flow into the joint by capillary action. Once cooled, it forms a solid metallic bond that holds components mechanically and ensures good electrical conduction. This 63/37 formulation is widely appreciated for its balance of performance, reliability, and ease of use, especially in conventional electronics repair or prototyping environments.
Eutectic 63/37 alloy for sharp melting at one temperature.

desc: The TIP140 is a robust NPN Darlington transistor offering high DC current gain. It’s ideal for power amplifiers and low-speed switching applications.

blocks.text: TIP140 NPN Power Darlington Transistor 60V 10A TO-247-3

The TIP140 is an NPN Darlington silicon power transistor designed for robust general-purpose amplification and low-frequency switching. Packaged in TO-247, the TIP140 integrates two transistors monolithically to deliver very high DC current gain with a single control input, making it suitable where large collector currents must be switched or amplified with modest base drive.

Thanks to its Darlington pair construction and built-in base-emitter shunt resistor, the device simplifies circuit design by reducing external bias components and improving stability under load. The transistor is rated for substantial power handling when properly mounted to a heatsink, and typical on-state voltages reflect the Darlington topology’s higher saturation compared with single transistors.

Mechanically available in TO-247 (the TO-247 package is the primary offering), the TIP140 targets power control roles such as motor drivers, power amplifiers, and switching regulators where a rugged, high-gain, high-current NPN device is required. Thermal and safe-operating-area graphs in the datasheet guide reliable use at elevated currents and voltages.

VCC is the power pin. You can connect it to 5V output from your Arduino.
GND is the common ground for power and logic.
SCL is the SPI Clock pin, its an input to the chip.
SDA is the Serial Data In (MOSI) pin, for data sent from your microcontroller to the MS5611.
CSB is the Chip Select pin. If you want to connect multiple MS5611’s to one microcontroller, have them share the SDA, SDO and SCL pins and assign each one a unique CSB pin.
SDO is the Serial Data Out (MISO) pin, for data sent from the MS5611 to your microcontroller.
PS is Protocol Select pin. Pull it LOW to enable an SPI communication.
SCL is also the I2C clock pin, connect to your microcontrollers I2C clock line.
SDA is also the I2C data pin, connect to your microcontrollers I2C data line.

CSB pin determines the I2C address of the module. When you leave the CSB pin unconnected, the default I2C address is 0x77Hex and when you connect it to VCC, the line is pulled HIGH and the I2C address becomes 0x76Hex.
PS is Protocol Select pin. Leave it unconnected to enable an I2C communication.

blocks.text: AT3503 Hall Effect Sensor SMD SOT-23

The AT3503 Hall Effect Sensor is a compact, high-performance linear magnetic sensor designed for precision motion, position, and current detection. Housed in a space-saving SOT-23 package, this device converts magnetic fields into a stable ratiometric analog voltage, making it a versatile choice for engineers and product designers seeking reliable non-contact sensing solutions.

Unlike simple on/off digital Hall switches, the AT3503 provides a continuous voltage output proportional to the strength and polarity of the magnetic field. At zero field, the output sits near half the supply voltage, ensuring accurate detection of both north and south poles. With its sensitivity of approximately 1.3 mV/Gauss, it captures even small magnetic variations, ideal for demanding control and monitoring applications.

Built around a microcontroller and high-current MOSFETs, the board delivers quiet switching and smart protection while presenting a straightforward physical interface: terminal blocks for motors and power, DIP switches for input mode selection, status LEDs, and on-board test buttons.

Designed with practical prototyping in mind, the MDDS60 accepts multiple control paradigms – RC, analog/PWM, simplified serial, or packetized serial – letting builders connect hobby radio receivers, potentiometer/joystick front-ends, or microcontrollers without redesigning wiring. Its on-board fan and thermal management reduce the need for external cooling in many setups, while clear LED feedback and tactile test buttons make bench-checking and troubleshooting quick.

The unit emphasizes reliability under load: it supports a broad motor supply range and high continuous/peak currents, includes under/over-voltage and temperature protections, and is packaged with top and bottom covers for safer mechanical integration. Its blend of power, protections and flexible inputs makes the MDDS60 a practical core for differential-drive robots or any project needing compact, heavy-duty dual motor control.

It packages robust MOSFET switching and onboard control circuitry into a compact board so users can connect a wide range of brushed DC motors directly to batteries or high-voltage supplies. The board’s layout groups power, control and output points for straightforward wiring and safe handling, reducing bench time during prototyping and testing.

Built to handle demanding loads, the MD25HV balances thermal management and current delivery through active protection systems and clear front-panel indicators. The manual emphasizes predictable, safe operation across a broad voltage range and gives wiring and startup guidance to avoid damage from reversed polarity or undervoltage conditions. Protective behaviors such as active current limiting and temperature-based throttling let the board deliver usable performance while guarding its power stage, making the MD25HV suitable for robotics and mobile applications where high voltage and reliability matter.

The FD04A Rev2.0 is a compact, user-friendly motor driver board designed to control multiple small brushed DC motors. The board is laid out so hobbyists and educators can wire motors and power quickly via screw terminals or a soldered bottom pad for higher-current runs. Visual indicators and simple test switches allow quick verification of power and output states without extra equipment.

Control is exposed through a 7×2 IDE socket (or optional extra pads) so the FD04A integrates neatly with microcontroller ribbon-cables or custom headers. Onboard logic circuitry includes a 5V regulator providing a convenient V pin for peripheral use, while the board’s physical layout groups power, motor terminals, and control pins to simplify wiring and bench testing.

The manual emphasizes safe, practical use – such as connecting motor power to the correct terminal, soldering heavy wires for >20A applications, and using the provided IDE cable for consistent control connections. The combination of accessible connectors, test buttons, and clear labelling makes the FD04A well suited for teaching, prototyping and compact multi-motor projects.

blocks.text: The MD30C is a compact, fully NMOS H-bridge DC motor driver engineered to control a single brushed DC motor. It focuses on efficient switching and thermal-friendly operation so that external heatsinks or fans are generally unnecessary. Built-in protections and flexible input options make the board practical for hobbyist and embedded projects. Its compact footprint and simple connectors make it easy to integrate into builds.

In standalone mode the board offers onboard switches and a speed potentiometer, with jumper-selectable inputs that let users choose internal or external control sources. Visual indicators and manual test buttons provide quick feedback and allow diagnostic checks without extra tools. The layout supports both terminal and soldered connections for different current-handling needs. This design reduces setup time and simplifies field adjustments during testing.

When used with a microcontroller, the MD30C accepts standard logic-level control signals and supports multiple PWM control strategies for smooth motor behavior. Thoughtful jumper configurations and startup recommendations help ensure predictable motor states such as braking or rotation direction. Clear documentation and jumper labels guide correct configuration so beginners can get reliable results. Overall, the MD30C presents a user-friendly balance of control flexibility and robust protection and reliability.

blocks.text: Cytron SUMO-BIT Expansion Board without micro: bit

The Cytron SUMO:BIT is an expansion board that transforms the BBC micro: bit into the central brain of a sumo robot. It is specifically engineered to simplify the process of building and coding for sumo robot projects or competitions. By handling the complex power management and sensor interfacing, it allows users to focus on strategy and programming within the micro: bit’s accessible environment.

This board is designed as a robust intermediary platform. It accepts high-power battery input and features sockets to plug in external MD13S motor driver boards, which handle the high-current demands of the motors. This modular design allows for easy replacement of motor drivers if needed. The board integrates all necessary components, including sensor ports, status indicators, and control interfaces, onto a single PCB.

The SUMO:BIT’s primary role is to provide a complete and protected ecosystem for a micro: bit-controlled robot. It safely channels power from a battery to the motors and processors, connects a suite of sensors for opponent and edge detection, and offers user-programmable LEDs and ports for additional servos or RC equipment, creating a ready-to-use foundation for robotic combat.

The Cytron MDS40B is an enhanced motor driver designed to control medium to high-power brushed DC motors. The driver features advanced smart capabilities, making it ideal for robotics and other motor-driven applications.

Equipped with MOSFETs switched at 16 kHz, the MDS40B ensures quiet operation. It also includes a microcontroller that manages key functions such as current limiting, thermal protection, and multiple input modes. The driver’s versatility allows users to control motors using RC signals, analog input, PWM, or serial communication, making it highly adaptable to different use cases.

The driver is built with safety in mind, offering multiple protection mechanisms such as under-voltage and over-voltage indicators, over-temperature protection, and an input error detection system. These features enhance the reliability of the driver, making it a robust choice for demanding applications.

blocks.text: DS8216D 4-Bit Bidirectional Bus Driver IC DIP-16

DS8216D 4-Bit Bidirectional Bus Driver IC DIP-16 is a high-performance 4-bit bidirectional bus transceiver designed for bus-oriented digital systems. It features four TRI-STATE bidirectional data buffers, TTL-compatible inputs and outputs, and high-current drive capability for reliable interfacing with memories, I/O devices, and microprocessors. The device supports bidirectional data transfer controlled by the DIEN input and device enable via the CS input. With low input loading, fast propagation delay, and compatibility with 8080-type CPUs, it is ideal for data bus buffering, interface control, and digital communication applications. The DS8216D corresponds to the non-inverting DP8216 family described in the uploaded datasheet.
TRI-STATE outputs for direct bus interfacing.

blocks.text: Cytron HAT-MAKER Simplifying Raspberry Pi Hat

The Cytron Maker pHAT is a specially designed add-on board that simplifies the process of getting started with Raspberry Pi projects. It directly addresses common frustrations faced by beginners and makers, such as the difficulty of headless setup without extra peripherals and the challenge of prototyping without clear indicators or easy access to GPIO pins.

Its core purpose is to enable headless operation, allowing users to remotely access and configure their Raspberry Pi through a serial connection over USB immediately upon powering it up. The board significantly eases prototyping by integrating visual and auditory feedback components directly onto the HAT, making the interaction with code and hardware more intuitive and educational.

Designed with a focus on user experience, the Maker pHAT features a Raspberry Pi Zero form factor for a perfect fit and includes clear, on-board labeling for all GPIO pins. It eliminates the need for external hardware for basic functions, providing an all-in-one solution that empowers users to jump straight into creating and learning without initial hardware hurdles.

The design reduces the initial friction of getting a Pico-powered project running by grouping common I/O and conveniences in one tidy board.

Its layout and on-board conveniences are arranged to speed up learning and experimentation: power and GPIO indicators, accessible headers, and user controls promote trial-and-error learning without complicated wiring. Labels, accessible connectors, and simple I/O access let beginners focus on code and concept validation instead of low-level hardware setup. name: TL7702 Supply Voltage Controller DIP-8
desc: TL7702 DIP-8 supply voltage supervisor with precision reference, adjustable reset timing, and complementary outputs for reliable system startup.

blocks.text: The TL7702 is a compact, integrated supply-voltage supervisor provided in a standard DIP-8 package. Designed for system reset control, it monitors a designated sense input and produces defined reset outputs during power-up and undervoltage events. The device integrates a temperature-compensated reference and an internal timer which, together with an external timing capacitor, determine the duration of reset assertion to ensure clean initialization of downstream logic.

In operation the TL7702 maintains the reset outputs active until monitored voltages exceed a precise threshold, then uses the timing capacitor to provide a controlled release. The device offers complementary reset outputs (active high and active low) with open-collector/open-drain style behavior that requires external pull-ups for logic-level signaling. Its compact DIP form factor simplifies prototyping and replacement in through-hole designs. It is tolerant of moderate supply transients too.

Engineers value the TL7702 for its predictable reset timing and the ability to adjust threshold behavior using a simple resistor divider at the SENSE pin. Built-in hysteresis and low reference drift across temperature reduce false triggers. The part’s documented thermal and ESD limits support safe board-level integration when layout guidance is followed, making it a straightforward choice for reliable system initialization in many designs.

desc: The U2164D is a 64K-bit DRAM chip in a 16-pin DIP package, offering 150ns access time and 128 refresh cycles every 2μs, ideal for vintage electronics.

blocks.text: The U2164D is a 64K-bit dynamic RAM (DRAM) chip organized as four 16K-bit banks, each 1-bit wide, packaged in a 16-pin Dual In-line Package (DIP). Manufactured in the German Democratic Republic (GDR) during the 1980s, it was produced by VEB Kombinat Mikroelektronik Erfurt (KME). This chip was commonly used in vintage computing systems and arcade machines.

As a DRAM, the U2164D requires periodic refreshing to maintain data integrity. It operates with a 150ns access time and supports a refresh cycle of 128 cycles every 2 microseconds. The chip’s architecture allows for efficient data storage and retrieval, making it suitable for applications where space and power efficiency are crucial.

While the U2164D is no longer in production, it remains a valuable component for enthusiasts and restorers of vintage electronics. Its functionality is comparable to other 4164-type DRAM chips, such as the TMS4164, MB8264, and MK4116, which can serve as direct replacements in compatible systems.

The P8050AH is an 8-bit microcontroller from Intel’s MCS-48 family, built on high-performance HMOS II NMOS technology. It integrates a self-sufficient 8048 CPU, 4KB of mask ROM for program storage, and 256 bytes of RAM for data handling. Designed for embedded control, it consolidates computing, timing, and I/O management into a single silicon chip.

Optimized for real-time processing, the device executes instructions in 1 or 2 cycles, achieving a rapid 1.36 µs cycle time at 11MHz. Its 96-instruction set emphasizes single-byte operations (90%), enabling compact code and efficient arithmetic/logic handling. The on-chip oscillator, timer/counter, and 27 I/O lines support autonomous operation while minimizing external components.

The P8050AH simplifies embedded designs with direct support for memory/I/O expansion via MCS-80/85 peripherals. It includes two interrupt levels and standby mode for power-sensitive applications. As a monolithic controller, it eliminates external memory needs for small-to-mid systems, balancing processing agility with hardware frugality.

blocks.text: LM1391 Phase-Locked Loop Analogue TV 40V 30mA IC PDIP-8

The LM1391 is a specialized analogue phase-locked loop (PLL) IC engineered primarily for the horizontal section of television receivers. It integrates a stable voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), a linear pulse phase detector, and a driver whose duty cycle can be varied by DC control. An internal active regulator improves supply rejection, while the output transistor provides low saturation and a high voltage swing suitable for direct interfacing with deflection and timing circuitry.

It supports automatic pulse control (APC) of the oscillator synchronized to incoming sync signals and yields a typical pull-in around 300 Hz with a hold-in up to 900 Hz, delivering robust lock performance. The balanced linear phase detector and low thermal frequency drift minimize static phase error, while adjustable DC loop gain lets designers tune transient response and stability for different receiver topologies.

Physically available in an 8-pin PDIP, the LM1391 includes application-friendly options such as an uncommitted output-collector pin for flexible interfacing and a regulator output for internal biasing. Typical uses are TV horizontal processors and low-frequency PLL tasks requiring precise timing and adjustable duty-cycle outputs. Its modest supply current and high-voltage output capability make it suitable for many legacy and industrial analogue systems worldwide.

blocks.text: UNI-T UT3550 Hand Held Battery Tester

The UNI-T UT3550 is a portable battery internal-resistance tester designed for real-time, on-the-spot evaluation of battery condition. It presents itself as a handheld instrument with a clear, operator-focused interface that guides users through measurement steps, zeroing and result storage. The unit is intended to simplify routine battery checks by giving immediate, easy-to-read feedback so technicians can quickly decide on battery status without lengthy setup.

Operation centers on a four-terminal measurement flow: connect the supplied leads, perform a short-circuit zeroing step to remove lead offsets, and trigger the measurement. The instrument’s menus and onscreen prompts walk users through calibration, measurement mode selection and saving results; data can be captured locally for later review. Its design balances handheld portability with workflow features found in benchtop testers, aiming to reduce measurement errors and speed inspection cycles.

The UT3550 emphasizes practical usability for field and production environments: it supports automated data recording, simple comparator-based sorting (pass/fail), and connectivity for remote control and data transfer. In short, it’s a focused tool for technicians and engineers who need reliable, repeatable battery checks with quick access to saved test records.

It couples an input LED to a light-activated triac output, providing galvanic isolation between low-voltage control circuitry and AC mains or power-triac gates. The device is intended to translate an LED trigger into a controlled AC-side trigger without the need for direct electrical connection.

Internally the device places the LED and triac-like detector in proximity so light from the LED reliably switches the output stage. The output element is designed to pass AC load current when triggered and to withstand repetitive off-state voltages appropriate to the model (S11MD5T rated at a minimum VDRM). Drawings in the datasheet show the pinout and internal connections so designers can place the part for straightforward gate drive routing.

Mechanically the component is specified with outline dimensions and soldering limits suitable for through-hole PCB assembly. The datasheet emphasises rugged isolation (high Viso), wide operating temperature range, and noise-resistant packaging to ensure consistent triggering of power triacs in mains-voltage circuits.

desc: TTL hex bus driver (NTE74367) with six 3-state outputs, active-low enables and non-inverting sections for robust bus buffering and multiplexing.

blocks.text: Hex Bus Drive with 3-State Outputs IC 74367

The NTE74367 is a TTL hex bus driver in a 16-lead plastic DIP package. It provides six buffered outputs with three-state capability to simplify sharing of common bus lines and reduce contention in multi-device systems. The device is arranged so sections can be used independently or cascaded, giving designers flexible placement for address, data or control signals.

Each section includes active-low enable (G) inputs that place outputs into a high-impedance state when disabled, permitting safe bus multiplexing. The outputs are engineered to drive common bus topologies and to interface with terminated lines, helping maintain signal integrity on longer or heavily loaded interconnects.

Emphasis in the device design is on reliable drive strength and input/output isolation, allowing improved fan-out and fan-in when buffering memory address registers, clock lines, or general bus interfaces. The through-hole 16-pin package eases prototyping and board layout while providing consistent timing behavior for TTL-based digital designs.

blocks.text: The 5KP22V is a high-energy transient voltage suppressor (TVS) from the 5KP series, designed to absorb large surge pulses and clamp transient overvoltages on power lines and high-power DC buses. It is part of a 5,000 W class of suppressors in the R-6/P600 molded package, offered in uni- and bi-directional versions. The device is engineered to protect systems from lightning-induced surges and switching transients by conducting the transient current to ground and keeping the clamped voltage well below destructive levels.

Mechanically the part is a robust, glass-passivated chip junction in a JEDEC R-6/P600 molded plastic package, suitable for heavy duty transient events. Its construction yields low dynamic impedance so the clamping voltage rises minimally as surge current increases; this lets the device limit the peak voltage seen by protected circuitry. The datasheet also specifies high-temperature solder endurance and reflow parameters for board assembly.

Electrically the 5KP22V is specified with a 22 V stand-off (VR) and a tightly controlled breakdown/clamp behavior at specified test currents. It supports connection in series/parallel to scale capacity, and is rated for very high single-pulse energy (5000 W peak power on a 10×1000 μs waveform) while providing fast response (<1.0 μs). These traits make it suitable for industrial and utility environments where occasional extremely large surges must be dissipated without damaging downstream components.

The device integrates flexible peripheral resources — including timers/counters, PWM channels, a byte-oriented USART, SPI, Two-wire Serial Interface (TWI), and an 8-channel 10-bit ADC — together with power-management modes and on-chip watchdog and brown-out detection to optimise reliability and power consumption for embedded control systems.

The ATmega8535 is backward compatible with AT90S8535 in most cases. The ATmega8535 provides all the features of the AT90S8535. In addition, several new features are added. However, some incompatibilities between the two microcontrollers exist. To solve this problem, an AT90S8535 compatibility mode can be selected by programming the S8535C fuse. ATmega8535 is pin compatible with AT90S8535, and can replace the AT90S8535 on current Printed Circuit Boards. However, the location of fuse bits and the electrical characteristics differs between the two devices.

Port A serves as the analog inputs to the A/D Converter. Port A also serves as an 8-bit bi-directional I/O port if the A/D Converter is not used. Port pins can provide internal pull-up resistors (selectable per bit). Port A output buffers have symmetrical drive characteristics with both high sink and source capability. When pins PA0 to PA7 are used as inputs and are externally pulled low, they will source current if the internal pull-up resistors are activated. The Port A pins are tri-stated when a reset condition becomes active, even if the clock is not running.

Port B is an 8-bit bi-directional I/O port with internal pull-up resistors (selectable per bit). Port B output buffers have symmetrical drive characteristics with both high sink and source capability. As inputs, Port B pins that are externally pulled low will source current if the pull-up resistors are activated. The Port B pins are tri-stated when a reset condition becomes active, even if the clock is not running. name: P8039AHL INTEL 8 bit Microcontroller
desc: Intel’s P8039AHL is an HMOS II 8-bit ROMless microcontroller with 128B RAM, 27 I/O lines, and a timer. Targets embedded control with external memory flexibility

blocks.text: The P8039AHL is an HMOS II-based microcontroller from Intel’s MCS®-48 family, designed as a self-sufficient, single-chip 8-bit parallel computer. It integrates a CPU, RAM, timer/counter, and I/O control on a single silicon die, leveraging Intel’s advanced N-channel silicon gate process. Unlike ROM-embedded variants, it omits internal program memory, relying solely on external storage for flexibility in system design.

Optimized for real-time control and arithmetic processing, the P8039AHL executes instructions rapidly (1.36 µs cycle time) using a lean instruction set dominated by single-byte operations. It supports binary and BCD arithmetic, bit manipulation, and two interrupt channels, prioritizing efficiency in embedded environments. The absence of on-chip ROM simplifies prototyping, allowing developers to tailor external memory to application needs.

Engineered for expandability, the microcontroller interfaces with MCS®-80/85 peripherals and external RAM/ROM via a bidirectional bus. Its on-board oscillator minimizes external components, while quasi-bidirectional I/O ports (27 total lines) streamline peripheral connectivity. The design emphasizes low-power operation, featuring RAM standby mode for data retention during voltage drops.
HMOS II Technology: High-performance, single 5V operation.
Expandable Memory/I/O: Supports external RAM/ROM and MCS®-80/85 peripherals.
On-Chip Timer: 8-bit timer/event counter for scheduling.
Dual Interrupts: Two single-level, maskable interrupts.

The HD14556B Dual Binary to 1-of-4 Decoder / Demultiplexer IC, available in a DIP-16 package, is a versatile and efficient component widely used in digital circuit designs. It has two select inputs (A and B), an active low enable input (E), and four mutually exclusive outputs (Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3). This IC is designed to convert binary input signals into one of four outputs, providing a powerful decoding function with reliable switching.

The HD14556B IC utilizes CMOS technology and is structured to operate with a supply voltage range of 3.0 Vdc to 18 Vdc. It supports active high or active low outputs depending on the application requirements. The device can be used for a wide range of tasks, including address decoding, memory selection, and demultiplexing. The decoder uses a simple two-bit binary input to generate one of the four outputs, offering efficient and flexible switching capabilities.

This IC can be easily expanded for larger decoding functions by connecting additional units, enabling complex decoding solutions. Its applications include digital data transmission systems, code conversion, and address decoding in both commercial and industrial systems. The device is essential for various control and automation systems where binary input must be converted into discrete, mutually exclusive outputs.

blocks.text: The JMX-94F-A-Z Latching Relay 12VDC 80A/220V is a high-current magnet latching relay designed for reliable switching in power control circuits. It uses a 12VDC coil and supports a heavy contact load up to 80A at 220VAC, making it suitable for applications that require strong load handling with stable switching performance. According to the PDF, the JMX-94F series is built with high sensitivity, high reliability, good anti-shock performance, and good anti-vibration performance.

This relay is a Single Coil Latching type, which means it can hold its contact position magnetically after receiving a control pulse. It does not need continuous coil power to remain in the set or reset state, helping reduce power consumption and heat during operation. The relay is pulse operated and designed for pulse control, with an ideal pulse duration of 50ms to 100ms for stable operation. The PDF also notes that latching relay coils should not be pulsed incorrectly, and the pulse width should be sufficient to ensure proper magnetic positioning.

The JMX-94F-A-Z model uses a 1A SPST-NO contact arrangement, with a dust cover enclosure and silver cadmium oxide contact material for heavy-load switching. The relay has an approximate operate time of 60ms and release/reset time of 20ms, allowing controlled switching in electrical power systems, meters, industrial control panels, and energy management circuits. With insulation resistance of 1000MΩ minimum, dielectric strength up to 4000VAC between contact and coil, and an operating temperature range from -25°C to +70°C, it is suitable for demanding control environments.

blocks.text: DRV8884PWPR HTSSOP-24-EP Stepper Motor Driver SMD IC

The DRV8884 is an integrated stepper motor driver designed for industrial applications requiring precise and efficient motor control. It features a built-in microstepping indexer, allowing the system to run with excellent performance at up to 1/16 microstepping resolution. With integrated current sense, the device eliminates the need for external resistors, thereby reducing board space and simplifying the design process. It operates over a wide input voltage range of 8V to 37V and can deliver up to 1.0A of continuous current per bridge, making it suitable for a variety of motor-driven applications.

The device includes a dual H-bridge power MOSFET driver with a simple STEP/DIR interface, making it easy to control the stepper motor. Additionally, the DRV8884 offers a selection of decay modes slow, mixed, and fixed off-time PWM chopping ensuring efficient and smooth motor operation with minimal torque ripple. This makes it especially useful in systems where smooth motion and reduced noise are crucial, such as printers, 3D printers, and robotic applications. The current is regulated without the need for external sense resistors, contributing to overall energy savings.

In addition to its precision control, the DRV8884 includes several built-in protection features like overcurrent protection, thermal shutdown, and undervoltage lockout to ensure reliable operation and prevent damage to the motor and IC. The low-power sleep mode (<20 μA) provides energy efficiency during standby. These integrated protections, combined with its robust current control features, make the DRV8884 an ideal choice for designs requiring both high performance and system safety.

The device is tailored for easy integration into applications requiring stepper motors but without complex programming interfaces, making it suitable for scenarios where a microprocessor’s burden must be minimized.

The ATD5984 operates with dual H-bridge output drivers that allow for precise current regulation in the motor windings. It features a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) current control mechanism, which ensures smooth motor operation by dynamically adjusting current levels. The device also includes features such as automatic detection and selection of current decay modes, including slow and mixed decay, optimizing efficiency and reducing audible noise. This flexibility is especially important in applications requiring fine control over the motor’s performance, such as in printers or small automation systems.

To enhance the device’s reliability, the ATD5984 includes multiple protection features, such as under-voltage lockout, overcurrent protection, and thermal shutdown. These protections ensure the system operates safely, preventing damage in case of faults. Furthermore, it incorporates synchronous rectification to reduce power consumption, providing efficient operation while minimizing heat generation, making it suitable for space-constrained or low-power applications.

name: UNI-T UT262C Non-Contact Phase Detectors
desc: The UNI‑T UT262C is a non‑contact clamp phase detector (70 – 1000 V AC) with 10–40 mm jaws, LED/buzzer alerts, missing‑phase and live‑wire detection.

blocks.text: The UNI‑T UT262C is a clamp‑style, non‑contact phase detector tailored for three‑phase AC systems up to 1 kV. Its jaw opening of 10 – 40 mm accommodates larger conductors and bus bars, enabling safe, hands‑free phase‑sequence verification without exposing users to live parts. The robust hinge and textured grip ensure stable clamping and one‑handed operation even in crowded switchgear racks.

Once clamped around the conductor, the UT262C instantly powers on and assesses phase rotation. Four LEDs illuminate in clockwise order and emit an intermittent tone for positive sequence; they reverse and produce a steady tone for negative sequence. Missing phases are signaled by an unlit LED, facilitating swift troubleshooting of open legs. After three minutes of inactivity, the unit auto‑shuts off to conserve its two R6 batteries.

Beyond rotation checks, the UT262C flags live conductors and broken circuits, and serves as a basic AC voltage detector (70 – 1000 V AC, 40 – 70 Hz). Its compact (70 × 75 × 30 mm), lightweight (≈ 180 g) design and simple LED‑buzzer interface make it ideal for industrial maintenance, motor installations, and distribution panel audits, eliminating the need for bulky testers.

Upon energization, the UT262A automatically powers on and begins monitoring the three phases. Four LEDs illuminate in sequence clockwise for positive phase rotation or counter‑clockwise for negative while an internal buzzer provides audible confirmation. If any phase is absent, the corresponding LED remains dark, aiding in rapid missing‑phase diagnosis. After three minutes of inactivity, the detector shuts off to conserve its replaceable R6 batteries.

Beyond phase‑sequence checks, the UT262A detects live conductors, assists in tracing circuit breaks, and supports basic voltage verification (70 – 600 V AC, 40 – 70 Hz). Its lightweight (≈180 g) yet durable plastic housing and straightforward LED–buzzer interface make it an indispensable tool for installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of motors, switchgear, and distribution panels.
