blocks.text: Voltage Detection Sensor Module Features & Specifications

The voltage Detection Sensor Module is a simple and very useful module that uses a potential divider to reduce any input voltage by a factor of 5. This allows us to use the Analog input pin of a microcontroller to monitor voltages higher than it capable of sensing. For example, with a 0V – 5V Analog input range, you can measure a voltage up to 25V. This module also includes convenient screw terminals for easy and secure connections of a wire.

The voltage circuit consists of a voltage divider circuit of two resistors in which R1 is 30K and R2 is 7.5K.
How to Use Voltage Sensor Module with Arduino

Interfacing a voltage sensor with Arduino or any other microcontroller is pretty straightforward. Connect the VCC and GND of the voltage source whose voltage is to be measured to the screw terminals of the voltage sensor. Connect the S and – (GND) pins of the voltage sensor to the Analog pin and GND of Arduino respectively.
Input and output voltage can be calculated using:
Vin = Vout * (R2/(R1+R2)) Here R1 = 30K ohm and R2 = 7.5K ohm Vout = (analogvalue * 5 / 1024).

blocks.text: UNI-T UT661D Series Pipeline Blockage Detectors

The UNI-T UT661D series are specialized tools designed to assist technicians in identifying and locating blockages within pipelines. The unit consists of two main components: a transmitter that sends a signal wire down the pipe via a signal wire, and a receiver that detects the signal emitted by the transmitter. This setup allows the user to follow the signal aboveground and determine exactly where the blockage or obstruction is located inside the pipe.

The device is engineered to handle various pipe materials including plastic (PVC) and metals (steel, iron), making it versatile across many scenarios. Its signal wire can extend deep into pipes up to 35 meters for the UT661D model while the receiver is capable of detecting the buried or enclosed transmitter through materials and soil up to around half a meter above the pipe. The design is meant for ease of use, with audible and visual cues to guide users to the blockage point.

Built to operate in field conditions, the UT661D is portable and reasonably rugged, with features to help its usability in environments like utility corridors, floor slabs, or buried pipelines. Its batteries allow for extended use, and its signal and alert systems reduce the chance of error in detection. Overall, the UT661D series aims to simplify pipeline diagnostics, helping reduce guesswork, speed up detection, and improve repair response times.

Its form is modestly sized and ergonomic long enough to grip comfortably, yet narrow enough to reach tight spaces on the bench. In ambient workshop lighting, the screen remains readable and uncluttered, with no superfluous controls to distract the user.

When the UT601 is powered on, it becomes a versatile instrument for assessing passive components. You place the test leads or clips onto a resistor or capacitor, and the meter quickly evaluates the value. It smoothly transitions among measuring resistance, capacitance, diode tests, and even checks transistor gain (hFE). The transitions are intuitive, and the display updates at a steady rate so that changes are reflected promptly without flicker or lag. Its “manual range” mode gives you control when automatic selection might misinterpret very small or large components.

In practice, the UT601 is a reliable companion on electronics workbench tasks. It does not overpromise it focuses on component-level measurements with clarity and consistency. Whether you’re validating a capacitor in a power supply, checking a resistor in a feedback loop, or diagnosing a transistor, the UT601 integrates into routine workflows without fuss. Though it lacks the sophistication of lab-grade instruments, its approachable design, consistent performance, and clear readouts make it a go-to meter for everyday component diagnostics.

The pair of RJ45 jacks sit side by side, enabling two separate network lines to be brought onto a single module.

When a network cable is plugged into either RJ45 jack, the signals (e.g. the eight conductors plus shield) are routed through internal PCB traces to the corresponding header pins. These header pins allow the board to interface with other modules, breadboards, or connectors without directly mounting the heavy RJ45 jacks there. The board serves as a mechanical and electrical intermediary, providing strain relief, stable mounting, and clear signal routing.

Used during prototyping, test setups, or compact network expansions, this breakout board allows designers to integrate dual Ethernet ports without fabricating custom PCBs. Its layout usually includes ground planes or shielding paths, and the board may also include LED indicator footprints or integrated resistor networks. The lightweight and modular nature of the board makes it easy to swap into existing designs, extend functionality, or debug individual network links without significant rework.

XIAO RP2040 is a microcontroller using the Raspberry Pi RP2040 chip, the first in-house designed chip released by the Raspberry Pi. Similar to the Arduino Nano RP2040 and Raspberry Pi Pico, the XIAO RP2040 is equipped with the same chip microcontroller RP2040.

RP2040 features a dual-core Arm Cortex-M0+ processor clocked at up to 133MHz. It has 264K SRAM and 2MB of onboard storage. With dual fast cores, plenty of on-chip RAM, and a port for Google’s TensorFlow Lite framework, XIAO RP2040 is a great platform for machine learning applications.

XIAO RP2040 is the development board of Seeeduino XIAO series. Like the Seeeduino XIAO, it is a compact board with multiple interfaces in a tiny thumb size and fully supports Arduino, MicroPython, and CircuitPython.

The rich onboard interfaces are enough for developing multiple applications. When you don’t need the size and power of a full Raspberry Pi, but don’t want to develop on the Arduino platform, the XIAO RP2040 is an excellent choice for running less complex projects.

XIAO RP2040 is a powerful performance and low-power microcontroller, which is ideal for various wearable and small projects. It can be programmed in C/C++ and the beginner-friendly MicroPython. And it has no components on the back, is breadboard-friendly, and SMD design, making it easy to use for projects.

In addition to the powerful CPU, the XIAO RP2040 has 2MB of Flash on board. 11 digital pins, 4 analog pins, 11 PWM Pins,1 I2C interface, 1 UART interface, 1 SPI interface, and 1 SWD Bonding pad interface. Some PINs have various functions.

Moreover, XIAO RP2040 supports the USB Type-C interface which can supply power and download code. 1 Reset button, 1 BOOT button, 1 user-programmable RGB LED, 1 power LED, 2 status indicators, and 1 user LED are on board, allowing developers to debug their code very easily.
XIAO RP2040 is compatible to the XIAO expansion board.
The XIAO RP2040 fully supports C/C++ and MicroPython because it uses the same chip (RP2040) as the Seeed RP2040 Microcontroller family.

Its body is cylindrical, tapering only at the end where the plating ends, and the joint to the heater barrel is smooth and uniform. The plating has a sheen, giving it a silver tone over the base copper, with a finish that feels finely machine-worked rather than rough or cast-grainy.

When in hand, the tip feels robust yet lightweight, designed for careful soldering work. Its bevel edge is crisp, which allows precise contact with pads, component leads, or wires. The copper base ensures that heat spreads quickly from the heater block through the tip; once hot, the plated surface helps reduce oxidation so solder wets more evenly. The plating likely adds resilience against the corrosive effects of flux and solder, as well as the elevated temperatures required in lead-free soldering.

After repeated use, the plated surface maintains much of its uniform look; wear tends to show first at the bevel tip edge. Cleaning (with sponge or brass wool) and tinning restore shine and keep the contact area smooth. The tip fits firmly in the sleeve of compatible 900M-series irons, so there is minimal wobble or misalignment. The finish suggests durability not a throwaway part, but one intended for repeated cycles of heating, soldering, cleaning, and maintenance. Visually and by touch it suggests a tool made for work: precise, reliable, built for frequent use under tougher conditions like lead-free soldering.

desc: Arduino MKR WAN 1310 offers secure, low-power LoRa connectivity featuring a SAMD21 processor and 2MB SPI Flash for advanced IoT applications.

blocks.text: Arduino MKR WAN 1310 LoRa Connectivity (Original Made In Italy)
Arduino MKR WAN 1310 allows you to build your next smart project. Ever wanted an automated house? Or a smart garden?

The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 board provides a practical and cost effective solution to add LoRa® connectivity to projects requiring low power. This open source board can be connected to the Arduino IoT Cloud.
Powered by a Microchip SAMD21 Cortex-M0+ 32-bit ARM processor at 48MHz.
Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa® module supporting 433/868/915 MHz carrier frequencies.
On‑board 2MByte SPI Flash for data logging, over‑the‑air (OTA) updates, and local storage.
ATECC508 cryptographic co‑processor for secure key storage and authentication.
Integrated Li‑Po battery charger with power path management.
Ultra‑low power consumption: as low as 104µA in sleep mode when properly configured.
8 digital I/O pins, 7 analog inputs (8/10/12‑bit ADC), 1 analog output (10‑bit DAC), and 12 PWM channels.
Micro USB port for programming and power (5V input).
Arduino Cloud compatible and supports LoRaWAN® protocols.

The MKR WAN 1310, brings in a series of improvements when compared to its predecessor, the MKR WAN 1300. While still based on the Microchip® SAMD21 low power processor, the Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa® module, and the MKR family’s characteristic crypto chip (the ECC508), the MKR WAN 1310 includes a new battery charger, a 2MByte SPI Flash, and improved control of the board’s power consumption.

The latest modifications have considerably improved the battery life on the MKR WAN 1310. When properly configured, the power consumption is now as low as 104uA! It is also possible to use the USB port to supply power (5V) to the board; run the board with or without batteries – the choice is yours.

Data logging and other OTA (Over The Air) functions are now possible since the inclusion of the on board 2MByte Flash. This new exciting feature will let you transfer configuration files from the infrastructure onto the board, create your own scripting commands, or simply store data locally to send it whenever the connectivity is best. Whilst the MKR WAN 1310’s crypto chip adds further security by storing credentials & certificates in the embedded secure element.
These features make it the perfect IoT node and building block for low-power wide-area IoT devices.

Check the Arduino Forum for questions about the Arduino Language, or how to make your own Projects with Arduino. Need any help with your board please get in touch with the official Arduino User Support as explained in our Contact Us page.
The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 is based on the SAMD21 microcontroller.

blocks.text: UNI-T UT25A AC Circuit Breaker Finder

The UNI‑T UT25A is an AC circuit breaker finder and GFCI socket tester designed for rapid and reliable identification of circuit breakers in live electrical circuits. The system comprises a plug‑in transmitter and a handheld receiver: the transmitter injects a tracking signal into the circuit, while the receiver emits audible beeps and flashes LEDs when the signal is detected. Sensitivity is adjustable via a combined power/sensitivity knob on the receiver, allowing precise pinpointing of the target breaker by reducing signal range once proximity is established.

The UT25A’s receiver also features line‑tracking LEDs to confirm continuity, while the transmitter’s GFCI socket test function uses three LEDs to display correct wiring or specific fault conditions (e.g., open ground, reversed hot/neutral). Housed in compact, lightweight enclosures, both units are powered by a single 9 V battery (type 1604/6F22) and conform to UL 61010‑1 and CSA C22.2 No. 61010‑1 safety standards.

Operating on standard North American voltages (90 – 120 V, 50 – 60 Hz), the UT25A is suitable for electricians and maintenance personnel in residential and commercial settings, providing a fast, non‑invasive, and user‑friendly method to trace breakers and verify outlet wiring without circuit shutdown

blocks.v: Vcc · The Vcc pin powers the sensor, DC3.3-5V
Trigger · Trigger pin is an Input pin. This pin has to be kept high for 10us to initialize measurement by sending US wave.
Echo · Echo pin is an Output pin. This pin goes high for a period of time which will be equal to the time taken for the US wave to return back to the sensor.
Ground · This pin is connected to the Ground of the system.

Digital signal output for distance measurement. · Connect Trigger Pin to a digital output pin and Echo Pin to a digital input pin of the microcontroller. · Used for triggering the sensor and reading the echo for distance calculation.

Allows communication with multiple devices over two wires (SDA and SCL). · Connect SDA and SCL to the respective pins on your microcontroller with pull-up resistors (typically 4.7kΩ). · Enables communication with multiple devices on the same bus using just two wires.

Serial communication for sending and receiving data. · Connect TX to RX and RX to TX of the microcontroller (with voltage level shifting if necessary). · Used for serial communication to transmit or receive data to/from the sensor.

A single-wire interface for multiple device communication. · Connect the data line to the Trigger Pin with a pull-up resistor (typically 4.7kΩ) to the supply voltage. · Allows communication between multiple devices over a single wire.
Echo Pin: 1kΩ resistor in series with the Echo Pin (if interfacing with a 3.3V system). · Ensures safe voltage level for the microcontroller (e.g., Arduino with 5V logic).
SDA/SCL Lines: 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors on both the SDA and SCL lines. · Required for proper I2C communication to ensure signal integrity.

TX/RX Lines: Level shifting may be required if interfacing with a 3.3V system. Use a voltage divider (typically 1kΩ and 2kΩ resistors). · Ensures the voltage levels between the HC-SR04 and microcontroller are compatible (for UART communication).
Data Line: 4.7kΩ pull-up resistor between data line and supply voltage. · Required to ensure reliable communication over the 1-WIRE data line.

blocks.text: Distance Measurement: The HC-SR04 sensor uses ultrasonic sound waves to measure the distance to an object. The sensor emits a pulse via the Trigger Pin. The pulse travels, hits an object, and returns to the sensor, which detects it through the Echo Pin. The time taken for the echo to return is proportional to the distance.

The transition from rim to center is smooth and continuous. If there is a handle or connector, it sits centered, almost like a gentle hilltop at the center of the dome, not jarring but integrated. In its quiet utility, it looks ready to cling, to adhere, to lift or to let go when needed. It seems like a tool of restraint and release, trusting surfaces and pressure to do the work.

The Jetson Nano Developer Kit offers useful tools like the Jetson GPIO Python library, and is compatible with common sensors and peripherals; including some new python compatibility with the SparkFun Qwiic ecosystem.

This kit includes everything you need to get started with JetBot minus a Phillips head screwdriver and an Ubuntu desktop GUI. If you need these, check out the includes tabs for some suggestions from our catalog. name: UNI-T UT12E-ROW AC Voltage Detector
desc: UNI-T UT12E-ROW is a rugged non-contact AC voltage detector (24–1000V) with LED, buzzer, vibration, flashlight, IP67 protection and 2 m drop resistance.

blocks.text: The UNI-T UT12E-ROW is a professional-grade non-contact AC voltage detector designed for safely detecting the presence of alternating voltage in wires and electrical installations without making direct contact. Its body is rugged and sealed to resist dust and moisture (IP67 rating), making it suitable for light industrial or field environments. The detector fits like a pen or small probe, allowing the user to move along cables, wall outlets, conduits, or junction boxes to sense live voltage via visual, audible, and vibration cues.

Internally, the UT12E-ROW senses the electric field emitted by AC voltage above a threshold. It alerts the user through a buzzer, LED indicator, and optional vibration feedback. The unit also includes a built-in flashlight for illuminating test points in dim or enclosed spaces. The design supports dual voltage modes (low and high sensitivity) to pick up both weak and strong AC signals, allowing flexible use depending on the wire under test.

In practice, this detector becomes a go-to safety tool for electricians, maintenance staff, and technicians before they work on wiring or electrical circuits. It helps to confirm whether a wire is live, identify phases or line presence, and provides a rapid check before engaging hands-on work. Because it is non-intrusive, compact, and robust, it serves as a convenient first line of defense for detecting dangerous voltage in residential, commercial, or industrial settings.
Maintenance & fault finding in wiring systems.

name: UNI-T UT12S-ROW AC Voltage Detector

blocks.text: The UNI-T UT12S-ROW is a non-contact AC voltage detector crafted to provide a fast and simple check for presence of live voltage in wiring systems, sockets, and conductors. With a slim, pen-style body, it slips into tool pouches easily and can be used quickly without needing to screw back covers or attach probes. Instead, by bringing it close to an electrical line or outlet, the user can detect whether AC voltage is present in a nonintrusive way.

Its detection system is based on sensing the electromagnetic field emitted by alternating current, which triggers LED lighting and a buzzer as feedback. The UT12S-ROW includes a built-in flashlight to illuminate test points in dark areas. Its design emphasizes reliability and safety: the unit is insulated, has an auto shutoff function, and is intended for repeated use in typical service and maintenance tasks.

In practice, the UT12S-ROW becomes a go-to tool when prioritizing speed and safety in preliminary checks. Electricians and maintenance personnel use it before performing work on circuits to confirm live status. Because it requires no contact and no complex setup, it’s ideal for quick walk-through inspections, checking wall sockets, junction boxes, and cable paths. Its portability and ease of use make it a practical companion for everyday electrical diagnostics.
Maintenance of low-voltage conductors, cables, sockets.

Encapsulated in a compact SOD-323 package, it is an ideal solution for portable electronics, communication devices, embedded systems, and industrial equipment where PCB space is limited.

The device is commonly used to safeguard microcontrollers, communication ports, sensors, and power inputs from potentially damaging transient voltage spikes.

name: EU to US Plug Adapter
desc: EU to US plug adapter: lets you plug European-round two-pin plugs into U.S. flat two-prong outlets; compact, safe, no voltage conversion supplied.

blocks.text: The EU to US plug adapter is a compact device designed to allow travelers and electronics users to connect European-style plugs (usually the round two-pin type) into American safety sockets that use two flat parallel prongs. It acts purely as a physical interface, enabling the prongs on your European power cable to align with the shape and layout required by U.S. outlets, without altering how your plug or outlet functions otherwise. The body of the adapter is typically molded plastic or similar insulating material, housing metal contacts inside which transfer current between the mismatched plug styles.

Inside this adapter, the internal conductors are shaped to bridge the geometric difference between round and flat pin designs. These conductors are often made of copper or copper alloy to ensure good electrical connection. There is usually a snug fit both where the European plug pins insert and where the U.S. flat prongs plug into the wall socket. The adapter is small just large enough to surround the metal parts safely and provide mechanical support, but designed to remain lightweight and convenient for portability.

Visually, the adapter tends to look simple: two round holes (for EU plug pins) on one side; two flat blades or prongs (for U.S.) on the opposite. Its appearance is utilitarian: compact form, often white or black, sometimes with slight markings or symbols indicating input/output and safety certification. Because it’s a bridge rather than a converter, there are no bulky components inside for voltage transformation. It must be used with devices that already support the local voltage range, otherwise supplying them could damage the device or cause unsafe operation.

The UT603 is a handheld instrument meant for measuring inductance, capacitance, and resistance in electronic components. It has a sizeable case, with a rotary switch to select different measurement ranges, and a large clear display to show results. The exterior oftentimes includes a protective jacket or grip-friendly surfaces. It feels solid when held, with the kind of heft that suggests durability. Even though its primary purpose is component testing, its design gives confidence that it can endure regular use in lab benches, workshops, or hobbyist environments.

Inside, the UT603 operates via a manual ranging mechanism: you must select the appropriate range for resistance, capacitance or inductance. The reading feels immediate once leads are connected and the device is switched to the proper mode. When testing capacitors, small inductors, or resistors, it resolves to expected values. While it does not measure AC or DC voltage or current like a full multimeter, its specialized focus gives cleaner, more reliable results for inductors and capacitors than many less dedicated tools.

Though its functions are specialized, the UT603 balances precision with simplicity. The user isn’t overwhelmed by menus range, mode, and component type are indicated clearly. The device is battery powered (standard 9V), so it is portable. Alligator clips or test leads are usually provided so that components or inductors can be clipped without needing extra tooling. The form factor is large enough to include a stand or support in some cases. Overall, the UT603 is a tool that gives good value: reliable component testing, ease of use, and reasonable build quality, especially for users who often work with capacitors, inductors or resistors in labs, prototypes or repairs.

Low quiescent current (~35–50 mA), wide operating voltage, and few peripherals make the TEA2025B ideal for battery-operated equipment.

With excellent channel separation, low noise, and soft clipping behavior, it delivers stable stereo audio performance in space- and cost-sensitive applications, providing an efficient and reliable solution for basic audio amplification needs.

name: Wireless Charger Module Power Supply Coil 5V 2A

blocks.text: Wireless charging technology can transfer power energy through medias such as air, paper, plastic, etc. This is a wireless charging module based on “magnetic-coupled resonance” technology that only consumes one-millionth of the power of traditional electromagnetic induction power technology. When the transmitter is electrified, it does not emit electromagnetic waves but forms a non-radiating field magnetic field around it. This magnetic field is used to connect with the receiving end and excite resonance at the receiver, by which the energy can be transmitted with minimal power consumption. Transmitting efficiency can reach up to 90%. What’s more, the magnetic field used in this technology is just as strong as the earth’s so it will not affect the human body or other devices.

This module is designed with the newly developed large current wireless power supply chip, and its circuit is pretty simple. Power the transmitting module with 12V, then the receiving end will output maximum 5V/2A power, which is applicable for small electronic products. Due to the non-contact charging design, the module can be completely sealed for being waterproof and dustproof, thus extending its service life and making it more convenient to use. The module can be used in phone power supply, portable device, 5V sensors, DIY wireless power, etc.
Note: It is recommended to control the load current below 1.8A if the module needs to work for a long time.

name: Light Sensitive LDR Relay Module 12V
desc: Light Sensitive LDR Relay Module 12V automatically switches devices based on light levels, using an LDR sensor and relay for automation in various applications.

blocks.text: This is a self-contained switching module that energizes / de-energizes a relay based on the the detection of visible light. Just add 12V power and hook up the load you want to control then adjust the potentiometer to set the brightness level at which you want the relay to switch between ON / OFF.

The Light Sensitive LDR Relay Module 12V can automatically control a load such as a night security light based on the ambient light level. The LDR sensor is attached to a 10″ lead for remote mounting. The lead can be spliced to increase its length if desired.
Automatically controls the relay based on light intensity
Included LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) sensor on 10″ lead detects visible light
Both NO (Normally Open) and NC (Normally Closed) contacts
LED indicator when relay is energized
The light sensor on the module is a light sensitive resistor (LDR) .
The brightness level trip-point for triggering the relay can be adjusted using the potentiometer on the module. Turning the pot CW increases the brightness trip-point.
When the brightness goes below the trip-point value, an LM393 voltage comparator IC energizes the relay and it switches ON. A blue LED is illuminated when the relay is energized.
When the brightness increases above the preset value, the relay switches back OFF.

The relay has both NO (Normally Open) and NC (Normally Closed) contacts so the module can either be used to energize a load when brightness goes up past the trip-point value or when it goes down below that level.

A flyback diode is included on the module in parallel to the relay coil to safely shunt current when the relay coil is de-energized. The module also has a reverse polarity protection diode on the 12V power input.

The module requires 12V power and ground to operate. There is a red LED that is lit when power is applied to the module. When the relay is de-energized it draws approximately 10mA. When energized, the module draws about 40mA from the Vcc pin.
GND = Connect to ground of the 12V power supply
The output of the relay is rated to switch up to 30VDC at 10A or up to 250VAC at up to 10A (See our notes below).

The output is SPDT type with both a NO (Normally Open) terminal and a NC (Normally Closed) terminal relative to the COM terminal. When the relay is de-energized (blue LED OFF) the NO-COM connection is open and the NC-COM connection is shorted. When the relay is energized (blue LED ON) the NO – COM connection is shorted and the NC-COM connection is open.
Top = Normally Open relay contact – Load is connected to this terminal if it should switch ON when relay is energized.
Center = Common connection – Connects to AC or DC power source for load that is being controlled.
Bottom = Normally Closed relay contact – Load is connected to this terminal if it should switch ON when relay is de-energized.

These are nice inexpensive modules that will work for many applications and allow you to control devices based on sensing light without the need to have an MCU involved. Just hook up 12V power and your load and you are all set.

The sensing works over a fairly wide range of light intensities. The potentiometer provides a relative rather than absolute setting, so setting the trip point will require some amount of trial and error. Positioning of the light sensor will also have an effect on the setting.
We do find the DC rating of the relay to be too aggressive. With DC voltages above about 15V, the contacts can become a little sticky. We recommend using it to switch DC voltages of no more than 15V.
With AC, the relays performed well in our testing. To test the upper limit we used it to switch a 1500W heater that draws about 12.5A and the relay handled it without any problems.

To test the device, connect it to 12V. While pointing the LDR sensor towards a light source, adjust the pot so that the blue LED just goes off. Shielding the LDR from the light should then cause the blue LED to turn on and an audible click heard from the relay as it switches.

blocks.text: The 6N135 is a high speed Optocoupler with Transistor output. It can switch at a speed of 1 Mbit/s with Bandwidth of 2MHz. It is TTL compatible with open collector output commonly used in Power supply circuits like inverter or in Data transfer circuits as logic isolators.

blocks.v: NC · No Connection – Cannot be used
Anode (A) · Anode pin of the IR LED. Connected to logic input
Cathode (C) · Cathode pin of the IR LED
NC · No Connection – Cannot be used
Ground · Ground pin of the IC
Output (VO) · Isolated Output pin of the Optocoupler
Base (VB) · By default it is enabled through a pull-up resistor.

blocks.text: Note: More details can be found at the 6N135 optocoupler datasheet which is available for download at the end of this page.

The 6N135 is a High Speed Optocoupler or Optoisolator. As we know the term Optocoupler/Optoisolater means we use light to indirectly couple (isolate) two sets of circuits. The speciality of 6N135 is that it has a high speed LED and hence can switch at 1Mbit/sec the output of the coupler is a TTL logic transistor making it easy to interface with other circuits.

The 6N135 is very similar to 6N137, the major difference is that 6N135 has transistor output and 6N137 has NAND output Enabling it to have high switching speed of 10Mbit/sec compared with the 1Mbit/sec of 6N135.

The maximum operating voltage of 6N135 is 15V and the transistor has an output current of 8mA with a peak of 16mA making it suitable to drive medium level loads. If you looking for some high voltage AC/DC switching try the MOC3021. Apart from that the IC also has an Enable pin which comes in handy while designing a strobe circuit for your camera flash.
So if you are looking for a high speed optocoupler for some digital applications like data conversion or noise elimination then this IC might be of interest to you.

Even though 6N135 is capable of working with both AC and DC it is commonly used with Digital circuits and works with 5V as supply voltage. A typical application circuit for 6N135 from data sheet is shown below

The Capacitor 0.1uF is a bypass capacitor across the Supply rail. The input signal should has an impedance of minimum 50 ohms with rise time and falls of 5nS of greater for the IC to respond. The input signal can be probed (if required) on pin 3 and the pull down resistor 100Ω is optional and can be used only if you are connecting the signal to scope.

As told earlier the output (pin 6) is an open drain transistor and hence it can either sink current or remain floating. So to avoid floating we should use a pull up resistor RL, the value of RL can be between 330 ohm to 4K depending upon the load connected.

The pin 7 is the Enable pin, this pin has an in-built pull up resistor hence by default the IC is enabled when powered. When connected to ground it will disable the output. The pin can be put into use to create strobe circuits etc.. The below truth table will help you understand the working of Enable pin.

Since the output is of open drain type, note that when the input is high the output will be low and vice versa. Since the IC is commonly used for fast switching another thing to consider is the propagation delay. When the input is logic on the output turn off only after (TPHL) and when the input is logic off the output turns on only after (TPLH). The same can be understood with the below switching diagram.

name: 7406 Hex Inverter Buffer/Driver IC
desc: The 7406 is a six-channel hex inverter buffer/driver IC commonly used for signal inversion, logic interfacing, and driving higher-voltage or higher-current loads.

blocks.text: The 7406 (ex 74LS06) is a chip with six open-collector inverters that has a maximum output voltage of 30V and a sink current of 40 mA so that they can interface with high-level circuits (such as MOSFETs), or for driving high-current loads.

When you have an open collector output, it means it’s easy to connect it to other chips that use different logic levels. However, it also means you can’t just swap it out with a regular inverter chip.

The 74LS06 comes in a 14-pin package, and you need to connect it to power before you can use it. Most 7400 ICs support a VCC voltage of 5V. One difference between the HC and LS versions of the chip is that the 74HC06 supports 2V to 6V, while the 74LS06 only supports 5V.

When an object contacts this roller, the internal switching mechanism is triggered to change the electrical state of the switch, enabling control logic systems to respond accordingly. Its construction combines metal bases with reinforced plastic housings, providing durability and resistance to everyday industrial wear and tear.

Built with dust-proof and splash-resistant sealing, the ME-8112 is suited for workshop, manufacturing line, and automated equipment settings where environmental contaminants like dust and moisture are present. The straight roller offers a smooth, linear motion interface, ensuring reliable activation even with slight contact pressures. This design supports consistent mechanical interaction between the actuator and the part being monitored, reducing false triggers and improving system reliability.

In operation, the switch provides a clear, repeatable signal whenever the actuator is pressed and released. Its compact size and straightforward screw-terminal connections make it simple to mount and integrate into control panels or modular mechanical assemblies. Although intended for industrial usage, its universal design also makes it a practical component for automation projects, test rigs, and mechanical safety interlocks where positional limits must be monitored and controlled.

The TEC1-12710 40x40mm Thermoelectric Cooler 10A Peltier Module is the simple application of Peltier Thermoelectric Effect. The module features 127 semiconductor couples in the area of 40mmx40mm.

Thermoelectric coolers also are known as TEC or Peltier Module create a temperature differential on each side. One side gets hot and the other side gets cool. Therefore, they can be used to either warm something up or cool something down, depending on which side you use. You can also take advantage of a temperature differential to generate electricity.

This Peltier works very well as long as you remove the heat from the hot side. After turning on the device, the hot side will heat quickly, the cold side will cool quickly. If you do not remove the heat from the hot side (with a heat sink or other device), the Peltier will quickly reach stasis and do nothing. We recommend using an old computer CPU heatsink or another block of metal to pull heat from the hot side. We were able to use a computer power supply and CPU heatsink to make the cold side so uncomfortable we could not hold our finger to it.

A thermoelectric cooling (TEC) module is a semiconductor-based electronic component that functions as a small heat pump. By applying the DC power source to a TEC, heat will be transferred from one side of the module to the other. It creates a cold and hot side. They are widely used in industrial areas, for example, computer CPU, CCDs, portable refrigerators, medical instruments, and so on.
Also Known as Thermoelectric cooling modules, Thermoelectric modules, Peltier modules, Thermoelectric cooling module.
Do not exceed Imax or Vmax when operating module.
Please carry out moisture protection options (sealing) in final application use.

blocks.text: The UNI-T UT658B is a compact handheld USB testing tool designed for monitoring and evaluating the performance of USB chargers, cables, power banks, and USB-powered devices. Rather than being a full multimeter, it sits inline between a USB power source and a load, letting you see how the voltage and current behave in real time. Because it’s small and portable, it can travel in tool bags or pockets and be used in labs, workshops, or field settings.

Internally, the UT658B senses the voltage at its input and measures the current flowing through it. It also accumulates charge (capacity in mAh) over time, providing insight into how much energy a device draws during a charging cycle. A simple button allows switching between memory banks or clearing data. Its visual LCD display shows multiple values simultaneously or in sequence, making it easy to compare metrics like voltage vs. current vs. total capacity. The inclusion of short cable makes it convenient to connect between devices without undue strain on ports.

In practical use, the UT658B becomes a go-to diagnostic tool for electronics technicians, hobbyists, or anyone needing to validate USB performance. It helps detect issues such as underperforming cables, weak chargers, voltage drop under load, or overrated power supplies. Because it logs data and stores multiple sets, it allows comparing charge cycles or evaluating power banks under different loads. While not replacing a full bench instrument, it fills the niche of fast, in-line USB power diagnostics with minimal setup.

Its small rectangular body houses an internal mechanism that can rapidly toggle contacts as soon as the roller lever is actuated. Because the switch is “SPDT” (single pole double throw), it offers flexibility to switch between normally-closed (NC) and normally-open (NO) circuits, making it adaptable to many control logic schemes.

Overall, the Micro Limit Switch Short Roller Lever 13mm 16A provides a reliable, snap-action solution for mechanical position detection, end-of-travel sensing, or limit detection in electromechanical systems. Its durable build, compact lever design, and high current capacity make it a practical component for appliances, machinery, or DIY electrical/electronic projects where space constraints and dependable switching matter. blocks.text: High DC Current Gain (hFE), typically 80 when IC=10mA
Note: Complete Technical Details can be found at the BD136 transistor datasheet given at the end of this page.

BD136 is a PNP transistor hence the collector and emitter will be closed (Forward biased) when the base pin is held at ground and will be opened (Reverse biased) when a signal is provided to base pin. This is where a PNP transistor differs from a NPN transistor, if you are looking for an equivalent NPN type check out BD135 transistor.

BD136 has a gain value of 40 to 250, this value determines the amplification capacity of the transistor. The maximum amount of current that could flow through the Collector pin is 1.5A, hence we cannot connect loads that consume more than 1.5A using this transistor. To bias a transistor we have to supply current to base pin, this current (IB) should be limited to 5mA and voltage across the base emitter pin should be 5V.

When this transistor is fully biased then it can allow a maximum of 1.5A to flow across the collector and emitter. This stage is called Saturation Region and the typical voltage allowed across the Collector-Emitter (V­CE) or Base-Emitter (VBE) could be 45V and 45V respectively. When base current is removed the transistor becomes fully off, this stage is called as the Cut-off Region and the Base Emitter voltage could be around 500 mV.

The BD136 is a medium power PNP transistor. It can be used to control heavy loads since it has a high collector current value of 1.5A. Another peculiar fact about this transistor is that it comes in plastic package, while most medium power transistor are available only in metal can package. This reduces the cost of the Transistor and also since the package is not conductive it will not be affected by other noise in the circuit. Due to this feature this transistor is widely used in amplifier applications.
So if you are looking for a medium power PNP transistor in Plastic package, then this Transistor might be the right choice for you.

name: RCWL-0516 Microwave Radar Sensor Module
desc: RCWL-0516 Doppler radar motion sensor. 360° detection, works through materials. Alternative to PIR, used in lighting, security.

blocks.text: The RCWL-0516 Microwave distance sensor uses microwave frequencies in a simple implementation of a Doppler radar. The circuitry inside the chip processes the signal and outputs an analog voltage that is proportional to the distance between the object and sensor.

blocks.v: OUT · Analog output from the sensor
VIN · Voltage input for the module

blocks.text: Components Present on the RCWL0516 Module
The following are the major components present in the module, which will be described later in the article.
RCWL0516 IC, transistors, capacitors, and resistors.
Note: Complete technical details can be found in the RCWL-0516 Datasheet linked at the bottom of this page.
The RCWL-0516 is a distance sensor that uses microwave frequencies in a simple implementation of a Doppler radar.

The antenna generates and receives radio waves from an object, which is then sent to a mixer. The circuitry inside the chip processes the signal and outputs an analog voltage that is proportional to the distance between the object and sensor.
Internal Circuit Diagram for RCWL0516 Module

RCWL0516 IC, which is a complete RF Doppler system in a chip is the heart of the module. The peripheral components act as power supply decoupling and filtering and set operating points. The RF section consists of a high-speed NPN transistor Q1, which forms a Colpitts oscillator. The antenna is a trace on the PCB.

The transistor Q1 also acts as a mixer that combines the transmitted and received signal and outputs the difference which is filtered by the low pass filter formed by C9 and R8, and is amplified by the IC. This signal can be treated the same way as the signal from a PIR sensor.
How to use the RCWL0516 Module?

The output of the RCWL0516 sensor is analog and can be connected to an analog input of a microcontroller and sampled by an ADC. The output voltage is roughly proportional to the distance between the sensor and the object. However, since it relies on a Doppler radar system, signal reflections from other nearby objects can interfere with the measurement, making it less reliable and accurate than other kinds of sensors. The reflections from different kinds of objects can also influence measurements, for example, metallic objects have a stronger reflection than plastic objects.
If the module does not output a signal:
Check if the correct pin is connected to the microcontroller
If the signal is intermittent or distorted:
Check the clearance between the sensor and the object to be measured and other objects.

The standard 5-pin through-hole design simplifies PCB integration, while its SPDT configuration provides flexibility in switching logic without requiring additional external components. With typical operating specifications suitable for many commercial and industrial environments, this Omron relay stands as a trusted choice for switching tasks where reliability and longevity are essential.

name: Lithium Battery Charger Protection Module (BMS) 3S 20A 12.6V
desc: This Battery Charger Protection BMS ensures safe and efficient management of 3-cell lithium-ion battery packs, offering robust protection against overcharge, over-discharge.

blocks.text: This Battery Charger Protection is a specialized 3-cell lithium battery protection board, engineered to act as an intelligent guardian for 12.6V battery packs. Its primary role is to continuously monitor the voltage of each individual cell within the series, as well as the overall current flow. By doing so, it ensures the battery operates within a safe electrical envelope, proactively preventing conditions that can lead to permanent damage or hazardous situations, thereby significantly enhancing the safety and longevity of the power source.

The Battery Charger Protection fundamental operation is based on a sophisticated protection circuit that automatically intervenes during abnormal conditions. It is designed to instantly cut off power if it detects an overcharge, over-discharge, or over-current event. This crucial function prevents the battery cells from being stressed beyond their limits, which can cause degradation or even thermal runaway. The inclusion of an auto-recovery feature means the system can automatically resume normal operation once the fault condition is removed and parameters return to a safe range, improving usability.

This Battery Charger Protection is built with a practical understanding of real-world applications, particularly for powering devices like electric motors. It emphasizes the importance of a proper setup, including using batteries with sufficient discharge rates and adequate wire thickness to handle the load. The design acknowledges thermal management, advising on load reduction if the heat dissipation is insufficient. Ultimately, it serves as a reliable, automated sentinel that manages the complex interplay between the battery, charger, and load to deliver stable and protected power.
Overcharge Protection: Prevents cells from exceeding safe voltage levels, enhancing battery lifespan.
Over-discharge Protection: Stops discharge when cells drop too low, preventing damage.
Over-current Protection: Limits current to protect against excessive loads.
Short Circuit Protection: Disconnects the battery in case of a short circuit for safety.
Cell Balancing: Ensures all cells charge evenly, improving efficiency and longevity.

blocks.text: The UT372 features a compact and portable design, with body dimensions of 184x56x34mm and a weight of just 100g, making it exceptionally easy to handle and transport . This technology allows it to measure rotational speed across an impressive range from 10 to 99,999 RPM, covering both very slow and extremely fast rotations . The device operates by reflecting laser light off a small piece of reflective tape applied to the rotating object, calculating RPM based on the frequency of the reflected pulses. This method ensures minimal interference with the machinery being measured while providing highly accurate results.

The UT372 is designed with user convenience in mind, featuring an automatic power-off function that activates after approximately 15 minutes of inactivity to conserve battery life . Its operation is straightforward, allowing technicians to quickly obtain measurements by simply pointing the device at the target and pressing a button. The inclusion of a USB interface enhances its functionality, enabling connection to computers for data transfer and further analysis using the included software . blocks.text: QTR-8RC Reflectance Line Follower Sensor Array

The QTR-8RC Reflectance Sensor Array is a compact module featuring eight infrared (IR) LED and phototransistor pairs mounted on a single board. These pairs are spaced at 0.375 inches (9.525 mm) intervals, making it ideal for detecting lines or edges in robotic applications. The sensor works by emitting IR light and measuring the amount reflected back from a surface—more reflection (e.g., from a white surface) results in faster capacitor discharge times, while less reflection (e.g., from a black line) takes longer. This RC (resistor-capacitor) version outputs digital signals that can be read via timing measurements on microcontroller I/O pins, eliminating the need for ADC resources. The board includes a MOSFET for controlling the LEDs, allowing them to be turned off to save power or modulated via PWM for brightness adjustment.

desc: HCF4511BE is a CMOS BCD-to-7-segment latch/decoder/driver (DIP-16) with lamp test, blanking and input latches; direct LED driving capability for displays.

blocks.text: HCF4511BE BCD to 7-Segment Display Driver IC DIP-16

The HCF4511BE is a compact CMOS BCD-to-7-segment latch/decoder/driver offered in a 16-pin DIP (and SOIC) package. It accepts a 4-bit BCD input and converts it into the seven segment outputs required to drive a single 7-segment LED display, combining CMOS logic for low quiescent current with bipolar output stages that can source display current directly. The device integrates input latches so codes can be stored and displayed independently of changing input lines.

The IC includes auxiliary control pins such as lamp test and blanking, enabling easy diagnostic testing of the display and blanking of segments when required. It also provides standardized, symmetrical output characteristics and balanced propagation delays to keep segment transitions even and predictable. Because the outputs are designed to source current, the HCF4511BE is especially suitable for driving common-anode style LED segments when used according to the datasheet’s wiring recommendations.

Overall, the HCF4511BE simplifies numeric display designs by removing the need for discrete decoder logic and separate driver transistors. Its latch capability and built-in test/blanking functions reduce external components and wiring, making it a convenient choice for counters, meters, consumer electronics readouts and similar single-digit numeric display applications.

name: L293D Shield for NodeMCU ESP8266
desc: L293D Shield is A motor driver shield that lets NodeMCU ESP8266 control DC motors and small robotic systems with simple GPIO signals.

blocks.text: The L293D Shield for NodeMCU ESP8266 is built around the L293D dual H-bridge motor driver, a chip designed to drive inductive loads such as DC motors, stepper motors, relays, and solenoids. The driver provides up to 600mA output current per channel, with 1.2A peak capability, and includes enable control, internal clamp diodes, and a separate logic supply so low-voltage control and motor power can be handled more safely.

In practical NodeMCU projects, this shield is used as a plug-in motor interface for Wi-Fi controlled cars, robot platforms, and automation builds. The referenced NodeMCU motor shield log shows it driving two motors using GPIO-based speed and direction control, and the project resources around it include a Wi-Fi car and an incubator controller, which reflects how commonly this part is used for remote motor control and compact embedded robotics.

This shield is designed for the NodeMCU V2 (narrow width), it comes with an L293D motor driver and breaks the GPIO to headers for easy access when connecting to various sensor modules. With the L293D, this shield supports the control of two (2) brush motor, start, stop, brake, direction and also speed. The shield also extends the GPIO of NodeMCU to header pins in SVG sequence (RC servo alike), not to forget the UART, SPI, Power, and GND pins. There are options to power the board separately or with single power source. The board also comes with a power LED indicator and a latching push button as a power switch.

In operation, the adapter maintains reliable serial communication at a wide range of baud rates, enabling legacy hardware to work seamlessly with newer computers. Whether you’re working in a lab, industrial environment, or running point-of-sale equipment, the converter cable offers a cost-effective and practical solution for integrating RS-232 systems into modern computing environments. blocks.text: LM358DR SMD Dual Operational Amplifiers SOIC-8

The LM358DR is a compact, industry-standard SOIC-8 packaged dual operational amplifier designed for use in single-supply and split-supply systems. Packaged for surface-mount assembly, the device integrates two independent, high-gain, frequency-compensated amplifiers in one small footprint, making it convenient for space-constrained PCBs where two op-amps are required.

Engineered to run from a single supply (and also usable with split supplies), the LM358DR offers stable operation across a broad supply range and maintains low quiescent current per amplifier pair. Its design supports direct sensing near ground because the common-mode input range includes ground, enabling simple interfacing to single-supply digital systems and sensors without extra negative rails.

TI provides the LM358DR as an orderable SOIC-8 part with standard surface-mount mechanical drawings and recommended PCB land patterns; tape-and-reel and other orderable packing details are listed in the datasheet for production assembly. The device’s long history and broad documentation make it a common choice for general-purpose analog signal conditioning in consumer and industrial products.

The IR2110 High Side and Low Side Gate Driver IC DIP-14 is a high voltage, high speed power MOSFET and IGBT driver with independent high and low side referenced output channels. Operating supply voltage range for IR2110 is 10 to 20 volt and output current is 2.5A. IR2110 comes in 14 pin through-hole PDIP package.

In many applications MOSFETs configured as high-side switches and many times it is configured as high-side and low-side switch. In such applications high-low side MOSFET drivers are used. How to use a Laser Diode?

If we want to operate a Laser diode then we must have laser diode driver circuit. As it helps in limiting current then supply it to laser diode. A laser diode can only work properly with the help of this circuit, if we directly connect it to the supply, because of having more current it will damage and if the value of current is low then the laser diode will not operate. Laser Diode driver circuit helps in providing a correct value of current to operate the laser diode. For making a laser diode driver circuit we need a few no. of components like resistor, capacitor and a voltage regulator IC.

The first capacitor in the circuit filter the High-frequency noise from the DC supply. The second capacitor works as power load balancer used to filter the fluctuating signals of output voltage. And a voltage regulator IC is used to provide a fix output voltage and we can adjust the output voltage by changing the value of resistor. You can use a potentiometer instead of resistor (R2) to adjust the intensity of laser light.

blocks.text: The XH-M452 Dual Temperature & Humidity Control Module is well suited for egg hatcheries, plant grow chambers and other enclosed spaces where you need to monitor and/or control both temperature and humidity of the air within the chamber.
Key Features of XH-M452 Temperature & Humidity Control Module
3-digit displays of current temperature and humidity
Operates in heating or cooling modes of operation

AM2120 temperature / humidity sensor w/ 36″ cable.
Note: Brand of Relay (Songle, Bestep, etc.) May vary from the picture shown according to the availability from the supplier. Please note it before placing the order

The XH-M452 module provides two separate control circuits with one based on temperature and the other based on humidity. The relays associated with each circuit can be programmed to activate or deactivate based on user programmed settings.

The temperature circuit can be used to control an AC or DC based heating or cooling element like a heat lamp or fan. The humidity circuit can be used to control an AC or DC based humidifier, dehumidifier, fan, water pump or other humidity control element.

The relays are used to make / break the hot lead connection to the device(s) being controlled. In the case of 120VAC, the black LINE is run through the relay while the white NEUTRAL and any GROUND leads connect directly to the device. In the case of 12VDC for instance, it would be the 12V hot lead going through the relay while the GROUND is wired directly to the devices and do not pass through this controller.
XH-M452 Dual Digital Temperature Humidity Controller – Sensor Opened

The AM2120 capacitive humidity/temperature sensor is on the end of a 1 meter / 3 foot cable. The cable is 4 wires, but only 3 are used. The sensor has a 3mm hole on the end for mounting. In most cases, mounting the sensor vertically such as on a wall gives the best reading. If heavy condensation is possible, it may be preferable to mount the sensor horizontally facing down to help keep water from collecting in the sensor and causing damage.
Air circulation within the enclosure is typically needed to ensure the sensor is reading the overall conditions within the enclosure.
A red LED on the left side lights when the temperature relay is energized. A green LED on the right lights when the humidity relay is energized.

The module itself is powered from 12VDC which is connected to the center screw terminal block. It draws approximately 100mA when both relays are energized. This power can come from an AC wall adapter or similar power source. If you are using 12VDC in your switching application, the module can be powered from the unswitched side of that power supply.
The module has two 3-digit displays composed of 0.36″ high 7-segment displays.
The left red display normally shows current measured temperature in °C while the right blue display shows current measured humidity in % RH.

When programming settings, the display will flash and show the current setting. Once you stop pushing buttons, after about 2 seconds the display will default back to displaying the current measured temperature or humidity and the setting will be automatically saved.
If you apply power to the module without the sensor attached or the sensor is defective or has a broken wire, it will display ‘LLL‘.
A display of ‘HHH‘ indicates the reading has exceeded the displays capability.
There are 4 buttons on the module that you can fiddle with. They are conveniently labeled in Chinese, so refer to the picture below for their functionality.
As might be expected, when changing settings the ‘+‘ increments the setting while the ‘-‘ decrements the setting for either temperature or humidity.
To restore to default factory settings, press both the two inside buttons (temperature – and Humidity +) for several seconds until the displays show ‘888 888’.
The default factory settings are to turn ON the temperature relay at 20°C (68°F) and turn it OFF at 30°C (86°F). The humidity relay is set to turn ON at 47% and turn OFF at 60%.
Short press to display current ON temperature
Long press (2 seconds) to set ON temperature.

blocks.text: Soldering Tin Paste is a mixture of powdered solder alloy and flux, designed to provide strong and reliable solder joints for electronic and electrical applications. It ensures efficient heat transfer, excellent wetting properties, and minimal residue after soldering. The paste is commonly used in surface mount technology (SMT), rework, and repair processes.
Solder Tin Paste allows for controlled and precise placement of solder on the PCB, which is especially important for small and densely-packed components.
The flux in the paste helps clean the surfaces, ensuring a strong, reliable electrical connection between components and the PCB.
Solder paste offers a more uniform heating process compared to other methods, reducing the likelihood of damage to sensitive components.
Lead-free solder pastes are available, supporting compliance with environmental standards like RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances).
It is easier to work with than traditional soldering wires or bars, making it ideal for automated processes.
Soldering paste is often more cost-effective for high-volume production compared to other soldering methods.
Solder pastes are generally composed of a metal alloy such as Sn (tin), Ag (silver), Cu (copper), and/or Pb (lead). Lead-free options are often based on alloys like SAC305 (96.5% Sn, 3% Ag, 0.5% Cu).
The paste has a specific viscosity that allows for easy application through stencils or syringes.
Flux is included in the paste to help remove oxidation from surfaces and improve the flow of solder.
The paste is formulated to melt at specific temperatures, typically around 183°C (for lead-free) or 183–190°C (for leaded solder) during the reflow soldering process.
Lead-free solder pastes have a melting point around 217–220°C.

desc: Compact mechanical vibration (SW-520D) shake switch, two-terminal sensor for tap/impact detection; operates −20 °C to +80 °C.

blocks.text: The SW-520D is a mechanical vibration (shake) sensor/switch designed to provide a simple, reliable on/off response when subjected to motion or impact. Housed in a small sealed body, the device uses a moving internal contact (a spring/ball or similar element) that closes or opens a circuit when shaken, making it ideal for basic detection of knocks, taps, jolts or continuous vibration. The sensor is intended as a low-cost interface between a mechanical disturbance and an electronic circuit, producing a clean digital signal that microcontrollers or alarm circuits can read.

Mechanically compact, the SW-520D is built for straightforward mounting and wiring; its two terminals allow direct connection to inputs or to simple conditioning circuits. The part is tolerant of repetitive actuation and is designed so that contact closure occurs predictably with defined physical motion. The datasheet notes that heat-shrink tubing is not temperature resistant on this part, so installation should allow for the component’s thermal limits.

The sensor supports a practical operating temperature window suited to many indoor and equipment environments, and it’s optimized for low-power, intermittent applications rather than continuous heavy current switching. The PDF specifies an operating temperature range of −20 °C to +80 °C, which frames typical uses in consumer electronics, alarm devices and light industrial monitoring.

name: 74162 Synchronous 4-Bit Counter 5V IC DIP-16
desc: TTL 74162: synchronous 4-bit binary counter with synchronous load, sync clear, dual enables and cascade output 16-pin PDIP/SOIC packages.

blocks.text: The 74162 is a synchronous 4-bit binary counter implemented in the TTL (LS) family. It provides four buffered outputs representing a 4-bit binary value and advances the count synchronously on a common clock edge when the enable inputs are asserted. The device supports parallel-loading of a preset value and a clear function, allowing designers to initialize or force any desired start count without ripple delays. Its internal gating makes all bit changes occur in the same clock transition, which simplifies timing in high-speed or cascaded counting applications.

Architecturally the IC includes parallel data inputs, active-low synchronous load and asynchronous clear pins, two enable inputs (for look-ahead expansion) and a ripple-carry / look-ahead output that lets multiple counters be cascaded for wider counters with predictable timing. Because counting is synchronous, hazards and glitches common to ripple counters are minimized; the outputs change in unison, so system timing and metastability are easier to manage.

Housed in standard 16-pin packages (PDIP, SOIC/SOP, CFP/LCCC variants), the 74162 is suited to TTL-based digital designs where a robust, easy-to-cascade binary counter is needed—for example frequency division, digital sequencing, timed state machines, or address generation in small microcontroller systems. Standard commercial temperature and packaging options are provided by the manufacturer.
Dual count-enable inputs for expansion/enable control (ENT, ENP).
Ripple-carry / look-ahead output for easy cascading.
TTL-LS logic family compatibility (5 V nominal supply).
Available in multiple 16-pin packages (PDIP, SOIC/SOP, CFP, LCCC).

It counts clock pulses in a decimal sequence from 0 to 9 and provides four parallel outputs representing the current count in BCD (Binary-Coded Decimal) format. Its synchronous design allows all four output bits to update together in response to the active clock edge, helping ensure reliable counting operation in digital systems.

This IC includes control inputs for enabling counting, clearing the counter, and synchronously loading preset data. These functions make it useful for building digital counters, programmable counting circuits, and timing systems. Its 16-pin DIP package is suitable for through-hole PCB assembly, educational electronics projects, and digital logic prototyping.

blocks.text: The SSR-40AA Solid State Relay is a single-phase electronic switching device designed to control AC loads using an AC control signal. Unlike traditional electromechanical relays, this solid-state relay contains no moving parts, resulting in silent operation, faster switching, improved reliability, and a significantly longer service life. This control method makes it especially suitable for resistive, capacitive, and non-saturated inductive loads. The SSR-40AA also incorporates high dielectric strength, excellent insulation, surge protection, and over-temperature protection to ensure reliable operation in demanding environments.

This IC features open-collector outputs, which require external pull-up resistors to produce a valid HIGH logic level. The open-collector configuration also allows outputs to be connected in suitable wired logic arrangements. Supplied in a 14-pin dual in-line package (DIP-14), it is suitable for through-hole PCB assembly, digital logic experiments, educational projects, and general-purpose logic circuits.

name: HC-06 Bluetooth Module
desc: HC-06 Bluetooth slave module: UART-to-Bluetooth link, Bluetooth 2.0 + EDR, 2.4 GHz band, default 9600 bps, simple wireless serial for embedded systems.

blocks.text: The HC-06 is a compact wireless serial interface module designed to enable Bluetooth communication between a microcontroller or embedded system and a master Bluetooth device (such as a smartphone, tablet or PC). It implements a transparent UART-to-Bluetooth link, meaning data transmitted into its RX/TX pins is sent wirelessly and received data is output on the serial pins, simplifying integration.

Engineered as a slave-only Bluetooth module operating under the Bluetooth 2.0 + EDR (Enhanced Data Rate) standard, the HC-06 abstracts away much of the complexity of wireless connectivity. Through simple UART commands and default baud rate (often 9600 bps) the module can pair with a master device, authenticate using a default pass-key (often “1234”) and then forward traffic transparently over the link.

Owing to its small physical size, minimal external components and UART interface, the HC-06 finds wide use in hobby electronics, embedded systems and IoT projects. It draws modest current, uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band (2.402-2.480 GHz), and allows devices without native Bluetooth capability to gain wireless serial connectivity. The simplicity of wiring and communication means it can often be dropped into an existing system with minimal redesign.
Transparent UART interface for wireless serial data exchange.

name: STC-1000 HW-524C Digital Temperature Controller 110-220VAC
desc: STC-1000 HW-524C controls heating and cooling with dual relays, offering precise temperature regulation for DIY, aquarium, and home automation projects.

blocks.text: The STC-1000 HW-524C Digital Temperature Controller is a versatile and reliable device designed for temperature regulation in various applications. Operating within the voltage range of 110-220VAC, this digital temperature controller is commonly used in home brewing, aquariums, and industrial applications, where precise temperature control is essential. It provides users with an easy-to-use interface to maintain specific temperature ranges for equipment, systems, and processes.

The STC-1000 features a digital display, which provides real-time temperature readings, and allows users to easily adjust the desired temperature setpoint. The controller also includes a sensor input, usually in the form of a thermocouple or NTC thermistor, to measure the current temperature accurately. Once the system’s temperature reaches the setpoint, the controller can trigger an action such as turning on or off heating or cooling devices, depending on the configuration.

One of the key features of the STC-1000 HW-524C is its dual relay outputs, which can control both heating and cooling elements independently. This allows the controller to maintain a precise temperature range by activating the appropriate devices based on whether the temperature is too high or too low. The temperature differential (hysteresis) can be adjusted to fine-tune the controller’s response, ensuring stable and consistent operation.

The device is designed to be user-friendly, with simple controls for temperature adjustments, settings, and calibration. It also includes various protection features, including over-temperature protection and overload protection, ensuring the safety and longevity of both the controller and the connected equipment.

In summary, the STC-1000 HW-524C Digital Temperature Controller offers an efficient, reliable, and easy-to-use solution for temperature regulation in a wide range of applications. With its dual relay outputs, adjustable settings, and robust features, it ensures precise and stable temperature control in diverse environments.
Dual Control for Heating and Cooling: The STC-1000 offers independent control of heating and cooling devices, making it versatile for different applications that require both temperature regulation.

Precise Temperature Control: With a digital interface and easy-to-adjust settings, it ensures highly accurate temperature control, making it ideal for sensitive applications like brewing or aquarium care.
User-Friendly Interface: The unit is designed with an intuitive and easy-to-use interface, allowing users to set and adjust temperatures without technical expertise.

Flexible Applications: This controller is not limited to one specific use. It’s suitable for a variety of applications including home brewing, HVAC systems, aquarium temperature control, and industrial processes.
Low Energy Consumption: The STC-1000 is energy-efficient, helping to reduce electricity usage by only activating heating or cooling elements when necessary.

Temperature Differentiation: The controller allows for adjusting the temperature differential or hysteresis, which helps avoid constant cycling of the heating and cooling elements, thus enhancing device longevity.
Safety Features: Designed with overload protection and over-temperature safety features, ensuring that both the device and the system it controls are protected from damage.
Compact and Durable Design: Its small size and high-quality components make it durable and easy to integrate into various systems, even in tight spaces.
Broad Voltage Range: With compatibility for 110-220VAC power input, the STC-1000 is highly adaptable for different electrical setups.
Reliable Performance: The controller is engineered for long-term, stable performance, making it a dependable choice for both residential and commercial applications.

desc: The IRFZ44 is a N-channel MOSFET with a high drain current of 55A and low Rds value of 16.5 mΩ.

blocks.text: The IRFZ44 is a N-channel MOSFET with a high drain current of 55A and low Rds value of 16.5 mΩ. It also has a low threshold voltage of 4V at which the MOSFET will start conducting. Hence it is commonly used with microcontrollers to drive with 5V. However a driver circuit is needed if the MOSFET has to be switched in completely.

blocks.v: Gate · Controls the biasing of the MOSFET
Drain · Current flows in through Drain
Source · Current flows out through Source

blocks.text: Rise time and fall time is about 97ns and 57ns respectively.
It is commonly used with Arduino, due to its low threshold current.
Note: Complete Technical Details can be found in the IRFZ44 datasheet given at the end of this page.

The IRFZ44 is known for its high drain current and fast switching speed. Adding to that it also has a low Rds value which will help in increasing the efficiency of switching circuits. The MOSFET will start turning on with a small gate voltage of 4V, but the drain current will be maximum only when a gate voltage of 10V is applied. If the mosfet has to be driven directly from a microcontroller like Arduino then try the logic level version IRLZ44 mosfet.

Unlike transistors MOSFET’s are voltage controlled devices. Meaning, they can be turned on or turned off by supplying the required Gate threshold voltage (VGS). IRFZ44 is an N-channel MOSFET, so the Drain and Source pins will be left open when there is no voltage applied to the gate pin. When a gate voltage is applied these pins gets closed.

If it is required to be switched with Arduino, then a simple drive circuit using a transistor will work to provide the required gate voltage to trigger the MOSFET to open fully. For other switching and amplifying applications, a dedicated MOFET Driver IC is required.

If the MOSFET gate pin is directly connected to an I/O pin of a microcontroller like Arduino, PIC, etc. Then it will not open completely and the maximum drain current will depend on the voltage applied to the gate pin. The below graph shows how much drain current is permitted for gate threshold voltage from 4V to 10V.
As you can see the MOSFET opens completely only when the gate voltage is around 10V. If it is somewhere around 5V then the drain current is limited to 20A and so on.

blocks.text: The 24C04 is a two-wire, 8-pin serial EEPROM IC. So if you are looking to use an EEPROM IC where low-power and low-voltage operation are essential, then this IC might be the right choice for you.
Interfacing 24C04 with a microcontroller is very easy as you only require to connect 5 pins. The interfacing diagram for 24C04 IC is shown below.

The Serial Clock SCK (pin 6) is connected to the Serial clock pin of the microcontroller, and the Serial Data SDA (pin 5) is connected to the Serial Data pin of the microcontroller. Also, like all I2C communication, SCK and SDA pins are pulled high using two pull-up resistors or while 4.7k. This will keep the bus at high state during the idle conditions.

Chip select pins (A0, A1, and A2) are useful only if more than one I2C device or EEPROM is connected to the same microcontroller, else three pins can be grounded directly. In the above diagram, we have connected the three pins to the GPIO pins so that we can cascade more than one EEPROM IC if required.

The Write Protect WP (pin 7) is provided for improving data security in the IC. The data can be written or erased on the EEPROM only if the WP pin is held low (logic 0). Else the data written on the EEPROM will remain as such. Normally this pin will be grounded (logic 0) when the protection is not needed. Data can be read from the EEPROM at all conditions irrespective of the status of the WP pin.

4093 – An IC with Four Schmitt Trigger NAND Gates
The 4093 is a CMOS chip with four NAND gates with a Schmitt trigger. Because each gate has two inputs and has four gates inside, it’s often referred to as a Quad 2-Input NAND Schmitt Trigger.

A NAND gate with a Schmitt trigger works more or less like a normal NAND gate. With the exception that the threshold for when it switches from LOW to HIGH is different from when it switches from HIGH to LOW.

blocks.v: 1, 5, 8, 12 · Input · Inputs A of the four NAND gates
2, 6, 9, 13 · Input · Inputs B of the four NAND gates
3, 4, 10, 11 · Output · Outputs from the four NAND gates

blocks.text: What is a NAND gate with Schmitt Trigger?
First of all, a NAND gate is a logic gate that works like an AND gate with a NOT gate on the output. Therefore it’s often called NOT-AND.
A NAND gate built from AND and NOT gates
This means that a NAND gate gives a LOW output only when all inputs are HIGH as shown in the truth table below.
Truth Table for the NAND gate
But this is a Schmitt trigger NAND gate. What does that mean?
This has to do with at what voltage the gate will interpret the input as a LOW or a HIGH input:

For example for a normal (non-Schmitt Trigger) gate that is powered from 5V, the gate might say that any voltage above 2.5V is HIGH, and any voltage below 2.5V is LOW. So if the input is at 2.5V and swinging a bit up and down (as these signals tend to do), then the output would be uncertain.
But for a Schmitt trigger gate, the threshold voltage is different based on if the input changes from LOW to HIGH or from HIGH to LOW.

For example, if the input is currently LOW, then a Schmitt trigger gate might require the input voltage to go above for 3.5V to switch to HIGH. But when it has switched to HIGH, dropping a bit below 3.5V doesn’t matter. Because in order to switch back to LOW, the Schmitt trigger gate requires the input to go down below for example 1.5V.

desc: CD4052BE DIP-16 CMOS dual 4-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer IC for low-power signal routing, switching, and conversion circuits.

blocks.text: The CD4052BE Dual 4-Channel Analog Multiplexer/Demultiplexer DIP-16 is a CMOS analog switching IC designed to control analog or digital signal routing using digital address inputs. It contains two independent 4-channel sections, commonly identified as X and Y channels, allowing paired signal paths to be selected at the same time. This makes it suitable for differential or dual-signal switching applications where two related signals need to be routed together. The device is supplied in a 16-pin PDIP package, making it practical for breadboards, prototyping, repair work, and through-hole PCB designs.

According to the datasheet, the CD4052B uses two binary control inputs, A and B, together with an inhibit input. These control signals select one of four channel pairs and connect the selected analog inputs to the common outputs. When the inhibit input is set to logic high, all channels are turned off, allowing the circuit to disconnect all signal paths when needed. The IC also includes logic-level conversion, enabling digital control signals to switch analog signals over a wider signal range.

The CD4052BE is useful in circuits that require compact, low-power signal selection, such as data acquisition, audio signal routing, sensor channel selection, and analog-to-digital or digital-to-analog conversion systems. It offers low quiescent power dissipation, low ON resistance, and very low OFF leakage, helping maintain signal integrity while reducing power consumption. Its break-before-make switching operation helps prevent channel overlap during transitions, making it reliable for precision switching and multiplexing applications.
